arXiv:1804.02306v5 [math.AG] 08 Feb 2021

Multipoint Okounkov bodies

Antonio Trusiani Note: antonio.trusiani91@gmail.com.
Abstract

Starting from the data of a big line bundle LL on a projective manifold XX with a choice of N≥1N\geq 1 different points on XX we provide a new construction of NN Okounkov bodies which encodes important geometric features of (L→X;p1,…,pN)(L\to X;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}) such as the volume of LL, the (moving) multipoint Seshadri constant of LL at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N}, and the possibility to construct Kähler packings centered at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N}. Toric manifolds and surfaces are examined in detail.

Keywords: Okounkov body, Seshadri constant, packings problem, projective manifold, ample line bundle.
2010 Mathematics subject classification: 14C20 (primary); 32Q15, 57R17 (secondary).

1 Introduction

Okounkov in [Oko96] and [Oko03] found a way to associate a convex body Δ⁡(L)⊂ℝn\Delta(L)\subset\mathbbm{R}^{n} to a polarized manifold (X,L)(X,L) where n=dimℂXn=\dim_{\mathbbm{C}}X. Namely,

Δ(L):=⋃k≥1{νp​(s)k:s∈H0​(X,k​L)∖{0}}¯\Delta(L):=\overline{\bigcup_{k\geq 1}\Big\{\frac{\nu^{p}(s)}{k}\,:\,s\in H^{0}(X,kL)\setminus\{0\}\Big\}}

where νp​(s)\nu^{p}(s) is the leading term exponent at pp with respect to a total additive order on ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} and holomorphic coordinates centered at p∈Xp\in X (see subsection 2.4). This convex body is now called Okounkov body.
Okounkov’s construction was inspired by toric geometry, indeed in the toric case, if LPL_{P} is a torus-invariant ample line bundle, Δ⁡(LP)\Delta(L_{P}) is essentially equal to the polytope PP.
The same construction works even if LL is a big line bundle, i.e. a line bundle such that VolX​(L):=lim supk→∞n!kn​dimℂH0​(X,k​L)>0\mathrm{Vol}_{X}(L):=\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{n!}{k^{n}}\dim_{\mathbbm{C}}H^{0}(X,kL)>0, as proved in [LM09], [KKh12] (see also [Bou14]) and the Okounkov body captures the volume of LL since

VolX​(L)=n!​Volℝn​(Δ⁡(L)).\mathrm{Vol}_{X}(L)=n!\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathbbm{R}^{n}}\big(\Delta(L)\big).

Moreover if >> is the lexicographical order then the (n−1)−(n-1)-volume of any not trivial slice of the Okounkov body given by Δ(L)∩{x1=t}\Delta(L)\cap\{x_{1}=t\} is related to the restricted volume of L−t​YL-tY along YY where YY is a smooth irreducible divisor such that Y|Up={z1=0}Y_{|U_{p}}=\{z_{1}=0\}.

Another invariant which can be encoded by the Okounkov body is the (moving) Seshadri constant ϵS​(‖L‖,p)\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p) (see [Dem90] in the ample case, or [Nak03] for the extension to the big case). In fact, as Küronya-Lozovanu showed in [KL15a], [KL17], if the Okounkov body is defined using the deglex order11 1 α<d​e​g​l​e​xβ\alpha<_{deglex}\beta iff |α|:=∑j=1nαj<|β||\alpha|:=\sum_{j=1}^{n}\alpha_{j}<|\beta| or |α|=|β||\alpha|=|\beta| and α<l​e​xβ\alpha<_{lex}\beta, where <l​e​x<_{lex} is the lexicographical order, then

ϵS​(‖L‖,p)=max⁡{0,sup{t≥0:t​Σn⊂Δ⁡(L)}}\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p)=\max\big\{0,\sup\{t\geq 0\,:\,t\Sigma_{n}\subset\Delta(L)\}\big\}

where Σn\Sigma_{n} is the unit n−n-simplex.
As observed by Witt Nyström in [WN15], one can restrict ourselves to considering the essential Okounkov body Δ​(L)ess\Delta(L)^{\mathrm{ess}} to get the same characterization of the moving Seshadri constant. This last object is defined as Δ​(L)ess:=⋃k≥1Δk​(L)ess\Delta(L)^{\mathrm{ess}}:=\bigcup_{k\geq 1}\Delta^{k}(L)^{\mathrm{ess}}, where Δk​(L)=Conv⁡({ν⁡(s)k:s∈H0​(X,k​L)∖{0}})\Delta^{k}(L)=\mathrm{Conv}(\{\frac{\nu(s)}{k}\,:\,s\in H^{0}(X,kL)\setminus\{0\}\}) and the essential part of Δk​(L)\Delta^{k}(L) consists of its interior as subset of ℝ≥0n\mathbbm{R}_{\geq 0}^{n} with its natural induced topology.

Seshadri constants are also defined for a collection of different points. For a nef line bundle LL, the multipoint Seshadri constant of LL at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} is given as

ϵS​(L,p1,…,pN):=infCL⋅C∑j=1Nmultpj​C.\epsilon_{S}(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}):=\inf_{C}\frac{L\cdot C}{\sum_{j=1}^{N}\mathrm{mult}_{p_{j}}C}.

In this paper we introduce a multipoint version of the Okounkov body. More precisely, for a fixed big line bundle LL on a projective manifold XX of dimension nn and p1,…,pN∈Xp_{1},\dots,p_{N}\in X different points, we construct NN Okounkov bodies Δj​(L)⊂ℝn\Delta_{j}(L)\subset\mathbbm{R}^{n} for j=1,…,Nj=1,\dots,N.

Definition 1.1.

Let LL be a big line bundle and let >> be a fixed total additive order on ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n}.

Δj(L):=⋃k≥1{νpj​(s)k:s∈Vk,j}¯⊂ℝn\Delta_{j}(L):=\overline{\bigcup_{k\geq 1}\Big\{\frac{\nu^{p_{j}}(s)}{k}\,:\,s\in V_{k,j}\Big\}}\subset\mathbbm{R}^{n}

is called multipoint Okounkov body of LL at pjp_{j}, where Vk,j:={s∈H0​(X,k​L)∖{0}:νpj​(s)<νpi​(s)​for​any​i≠j}V_{k,j}:=\{{s\in H^{0}(X,kL)\setminus\{0\}}\,:\,\nu^{p_{j}}(s)<\nu^{p_{i}}(s)\,\mathrm{for}\,\mathrm{any}\,i\neq j\} for any k≥1k\geq 1.

We observe that the multipoint Okounkov body of LL at pjp_{j} is obtained by considering all sections whose leading term in pjp_{j} is strictly smaller than those at the other points.
They are convex compact sets in ℝn\mathbbm{R}^{n} but, unlike the one-point case, for N≥2N\geq 2 it can happen that some Δj​(L)\Delta_{j}(L) are empty (Remark 3.8). The definition does not depend on the order of the points.

Our first theorem concerns the relationship between the multipoint Okounkov bodies and the volume of the line bundle:

Theorem A.
22 2 The theorem holds in the more general setting of a family of faithful valuations νpj:𝒪X,pj∖{0}→(ℤn,>)\nu^{p_{j}}:\mathcal{O}_{X,p_{j}}\setminus\{0\}\to(\mathbbm{Z}^{n},>) respect to a fixed total additive order >> on ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n}.

Let LL be a big line bundle. Then

n!​∑j=1NVolℝn​(Δj​(L))=VolX​(L).n!\sum_{j=1}^{N}\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathbbm{R}^{n}}\big(\Delta_{j}(L)\big)=\mathrm{Vol}_{X}(L).

Furthermore, similar to section §44 in [LM09], we show that Δj​(⋅)\Delta_{j}(\cdot) is a numerical invariant and that there exists an open subset of the big cone containing B+​(pj)C={α∈N1​(X)ℝ:pj∉𝔹+​(α)}B_{+}(p_{j})^{C}=\{{\alpha\in N^{1}(X)_{\mathbbm{R}}}\,:\,p_{j}\notin\mathbbm{B}_{+}(\alpha)\} over which Δj​(⋅)\Delta_{j}(\cdot) can be extended continuously (see section §3.2). Recall that the points, and more in general the valuations νpj\nu^{p_{j}}, are fixed.
Moreover when >> is the lexicographical order and Y1,…,YNY_{1},\dots,Y_{N} are smooth irreducible divisors such that Yj|Upj={zj,1=0}Y_{j|U_{p_{j}}}=\{z_{j,1}=0\}, the fibers of Δj​(L)\Delta_{j}(L) are related to the restricted volumes of L−t​∑i=1NYiL-t\sum_{i=1}^{N}Y_{i} along YjY_{j} (see section§3.3).

The multipoint Okounkov bodies can be finer invariants than the moving multipoint Seshadri constant (a natural generalization of the multipoint Seshadri constant to big line bundles, see section §\lx@sectionsign 5) as our next Theorem shows.

Theorem B.

Let LL be a big line bundle and let >> be the deglex order. Then

ϵS​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN)=max⁡{0,ξ⁡(L,p1,…,pN)}\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})=\max\big\{0,\xi(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})\big\}

where ξ(L;p1,…,pN):=sup{t≥0:tΣn⊂Δj(L)essforanyj=1,…,N}\xi(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}):=\sup\{t\geq 0\,:\,t\Sigma_{n}\subset\Delta_{j}(L)^{\mathrm{ess}}\,\mathrm{for}\,\mathrm{any}\,{j=1,\dots,N}\}.

Next we recall another interpretation of the one point Seshadri constant: ϵS​(L,p)\epsilon_{S}(L;p) is equal to the supremum of rr such that there exists an holomorphic embedding f:(Br​(0),ωs​t)→(X,L)f:(B_{r}(0),\omega_{st})\to(X,L) with the property that f∗​ωs​tf_{*}\omega_{st} extends to a Kähler form ω\omega with cohomology class c1​(L)c_{1}(L) (see Theorem 5.1.22 and Proposition 5.3.17. in [Laz04]). This result is a consequence of a deep analysis in symplectic geometry by McDuff-Polterovich ([MP94]), where they dealt with the symplectic packings problem (in the same spirit, Biran in [Bir97] proved the symplectic analog of the Nagata’s conjecture).
Subsequently Kaveh in [Kav16] showed how the one-point Okounkov body can be used to construct a sympletic packing. Along the same lines Witt Nyström in [WN15] introduced the torus-invariant domain Ω⁡(L):=μ−1​(Δ​(L)ess)\Omega(L):=\mu^{-1}\big(\Delta(L)^{\mathrm{ess}}\big) (called Okounkov domain) for μ:ℂn→ℝn\mu:\mathbbm{C}^{n}\to\mathbbm{R}^{n}, μ⁡(z1,…,zn):=(|z1|2,…,|zn|2)\mu(z_{1},\dots,z_{n}):=(\lvert z_{1}\rvert^{2},\dots,\lvert z_{n}\rvert^{2}), and showed how it approximates the polarized manifold.

To get a similar characterization of the multipoint Seshadri constant, we give the following definition of Kähler packing.

Definition 1.2.

We say that a finite family of n−n-dimensional Kähler manifolds {(Mj,ηj)}j=1N\{(M_{j},\eta_{j})\}_{j=1}^{N} packs into (X,L)(X,L) for LL ample line bundle on a n−n-dimensional projective manifold XX if for any family of relatively compact open set Uj⋐MjU_{j}\Subset M_{j} there are a holomorphic embedding f:⨆j=1NUj→Xf:\bigsqcup_{j=1}^{N}U_{j}\to X and a Kähler form ω\omega lying in c1​(L)c_{1}(L) such that f∗ηj=ω|f(Uj)f_{*}\eta_{j}=\omega_{|f(U_{j})}. If, in addition,

∑j=1N∫Mjηjn=∫Xc1​(L)n\sum_{j=1}^{N}\int_{M_{j}}\eta_{j}^{n}=\int_{X}c_{1}(L)^{n}

then we say that {(Mj,ηj)}j=1N\{(M_{j},\eta_{j})\}_{j=1}^{N} packs perfectly into (X,L)(X,L).

Following [WN15] we define the multipoint Okounkov domains as the torus-invariant domains of ℂn\mathbbm{C}^{n} given by Ωj​(L):=μ−1​(Δj​(L)ess)\Omega_{j}(L):=\mu^{-1}\big(\Delta_{j}(L)^{\mathrm{ess}}\big).

Theorem C.
33 3 the theorem holds even if νpj\nu^{p_{j}} is a family of faithful quasi-monomial valuations respect to the same linearly independent vectors λ→1,…,λ→n∈ℕn\vec{\lambda}_{1},\dots,\vec{\lambda}_{n}\in\mathbbm{N}^{n}.

Let LL be an ample line bundle. Then {(Ωj​(L),ωs​t)}j=1,…,N\{(\Omega_{j}(L),\omega_{st})\}_{j=1,\dots,N} packs perfectly into (X,L)(X,L).

Note that for big line bundles a similar theorem holds, given a slightly different definition of packings (see section 4.2).
As a consequence of Theorems B, 3 (see Corollary 5.15),

ϵS​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN)=max⁡{0,sup{r>0:{(Br​(0),ωs​t​d)}j=1N​packs into​(X,L)}}.\sqrt{\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})}=\max\Big\{0,\sup\big\{r>0\,:\,\{(B_{r}(0),\omega_{std}\big)\}_{j=1}^{N}\,\mbox{packs into}\,(X,L)\,\big\}\Big\}.

This result was known in dimension 22 by the work of Eckl ([Eckl17]), and for N=1N=1 by [WN15].

Moving to particular cases, for toric manifolds we prove that, chosen torus-fixed points and the deglex order, the multipoint Okounkov bodies can be obtained subdiving the polytope (Theorem 6.4). If we consider all torus-invariant points the subdivision is barycentric (Corollary 6.6). As a consequence we get that the multipoint Seshadri constant of NN torus-fixed points is in 12​ℕ\frac{1}{2}\mathbbm{N} (Corollary 6.7).

Finally in the surface case, we extend the result in [KLM12] showing, for the lexicographical order, the polyhedrality of Δj​(L)\Delta_{j}(L) (Theorem 6.9). Moreover for 𝒪ℙ2​(1)\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1) over ℙ2\mathbbm{P}^{2} we completely characterize Δj​(𝒪ℙ2​(1))\Delta_{j}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1)) in function of ϵS​(𝒪ℙ2​(1),N)\epsilon_{S}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1);N) obtaining an explicit formula for the restricted volume of μ∗​𝒪ℙ2​(1)−t​𝔼\mu^{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1)-t\mathbbm{E} for t∈ℚt\in\mathbbm{Q} where μ:X~→X\mu:\tilde{X}\to X is the blow-up at NN very general points and 𝔼:=∑j=1NEj\mathbbm{E}:=\sum_{j=1}^{N}E_{j} is the sum of the exceptional divisors (Theorem 6.14). As a consequence we independently get a result present in [DKMS15]: the ray μ∗​𝒪ℙ2​(1)−t​𝔼\mu^{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1)-t\mathbbm{E} meets at most two Zariski chambers.

1.1 Organization

Section 2 contains some preliminary facts on singular metrics, base loci of divisors and Okounkov bodies.
In section 3 we develop the theory of multipoint Okounkov bodies: the goal is to generalize some results in [LM09] for N≥1N\geq 1. We prove here Theorem A.
Section 4 is dedicated to show Theorem 3.
In section 5 we introduce the notion of moving multipoint Seshadri constants. Moreover we prove Theorem B, connecting the moving multipoint Seshadri constant in a more analytical language in the spirit of [Dem90], and deduce the connection between the moving multipoint Seshadri constant and Kähler packings.
The last section 6 deals with the two aforementioned particular cases: toric manifolds and surfaces.

1.2 Related works

In addition to the already mentioned papers of Witt Nyström ([WN15]), Eckl ([Eckl17]), and Kürona-Lozovanu ([KL15a], [KL17]), during the final revision of this paper the work of Shin [Sh17] appeared as a preprint. Starting from the same data of a big divisor over a projective manifold of dimension nn and the choice of rr different points, he gave a construction of an extended Okounkov Body ΔY⋅1,…,Y⋅r​(D)⊂ℝr​n\Delta_{Y_{\cdot}^{1},\dots,Y_{\cdot}^{r}}(D)\subset\mathbbm{R}^{rn} from a valuation associated to a family of admissible or infinitesimal flags Y⋅1,…,Y⋅rY_{\cdot}^{1},\dots,Y_{\cdot}^{r}. In the ample case thanks to the Serre’s vanishing Theorem, the multipoint Okounkov bodies can be recovered from the extended Okounkov body as projections after suitable subdivisions. Precisely, with the notation given in [Sh17], we get

F⁡(Δj​(D))=πj​(ΔY⋅1,…,Y⋅r​(D)∩H1,j∩⋯∩Hj−1,j∩Hj+1,j∩⋯∩Hr,j)F(\Delta_{j}(D))=\pi_{j}\Big(\Delta_{Y_{\cdot}^{1},\dots,Y_{\cdot}^{r}}(D)\cap H_{1,j}\cap\cdots\cap H_{j-1,j}\cap H_{j+1,j}\cap\cdots\cap H_{r,j}\Big)

where πj:ℝr​n→ℝn,πj​(x→1,…,x→r):=x→j\pi_{j}:\mathbbm{R}^{rn}\to\mathbbm{R}^{n},\pi_{j}(\vec{x}_{1},\dots,\vec{x}_{r}):=\vec{x}_{j}, Hi,j:={(x→1,…,x→r)∈ℝr​n:xi,1≥xj,1}H_{i,j}:=\{(\vec{x}_{1},\dots,\vec{x}_{r}){\in\mathbbm{R}^{rn}}\,:\,x_{i,1}\geq x_{j,1}\} and F:ℝn→ℝn,F⁡(y1,…,yn):=(|y|,y1,…,yn−1)F:\mathbbm{R}^{n}\to\mathbbm{R}^{n},F(y_{1},\dots,y_{n}):=(\lvert y\rvert,y_{1},\dots,y_{n-1}). Note that xi,1x_{i,1} means the first component of the vector xi→\vec{x_{i}} while |y|=y1+⋯+yn|y|=y_{1}+\dots+y_{n}. The same equality holds if L:=𝒪X​(D)L:=\mathcal{O}_{X}(D) is big and c1​(L)∈Supp​(Γj​(X))∘c_{1}(L)\in\mathrm{Supp}(\Gamma_{j}(X))^{\circ} (see section 3.2).

2 Preliminaries

2.1 Singular metrics and (currents of) curvature

Let LL be a holomorphic line bundle over a projective manifold XX. A smooth (hermitian) metric φ\varphi is the collection of an open cover {Uj}j∈J\{U_{j}\}_{j\in J} of XX and of smooth functions φj∈𝒞∞​(Uj)\varphi_{j}\in\mathcal{C}^{\infty}(U_{j}) such that on each not-empty intersection Ui∩UjU_{i}\cap U_{j} one has φi=φj+ln⁡|gi,j|2\varphi_{i}=\varphi_{j}+\ln|g_{i,j}|^{2} where gi,jg_{i,j} are the transition function defining the line bundle LL. Note that if sjs_{j} are nowhere zero local sections with respect to which the transition function are calculated then |sj|=e−φj|s_{j}|=e^{-\varphi_{j}}. The curvature of a smooth metric φ\varphi is given on each open UjU_{j} by d​dc​φjdd^{c}\varphi_{j} where dc=i4​π(∂−∂¯)d^{c}=\frac{i}{4\pi}(\partial-\bar{\partial}) so that d​dc=i2​π​∂∂¯dd^{c}=\frac{i}{2\pi}\partial\bar{\partial}. It is a global (1,1)−(1,1)-form on XX, so for convenience we use the notation d​dc​φdd^{c}\varphi. The metric is called positive if the (1,1)−(1,1)-form d​dc​φdd^{c}\varphi is a Kähler form, i.e. if the functions φj\varphi_{j} are strictly plurisubharmonic. By the well-known Kodaira Embedding Theorem, a line bundle admits a positive metric iff it is ample.
Demailly in [Dem90] introduced a weaker notion of metric: a (hermitian) singular metric φ\varphi is given by a collection of data as before but with the weaker condition that φj∈Ll​o​c1​(Uj)\varphi_{j}\in L^{1}_{loc}(U_{j}). If the functions φj\varphi_{j} are also plurisubharmonic, then we say that φ\varphi is a singular positive metric. Note that d​dc​φdd^{c}\varphi exists in the weak sense, indeed it is a closed positive (1,1)−(1,1)-current (we will call it the current of curvature of the metric φ\varphi). We say that d​dc​φdd^{c}\varphi is a Kähler current if it dominates some Kähler form ω\omega. By Proposition 4.2.4.2. in [Dem90] a line bundle is big iff it admits a singular positive metric whose current of curvature is a Kähler current.
In this paper we will often work with ℝ−\mathbbm{R}-line bundles, i.e. formal linear combinations of line bundles. Moreover since we will only consider projective manifolds, we will often identify an ℝ−\mathbbm{R}-line bundle as a class of ℝ−\mathbbm{R}-divisors modulo linear equivalence and its first Chern class as a class of ℝ−\mathbbm{R}-divisors modulo numerical equivalence.

2.2 Base loci

We recall here the construction of the base loci (see [ELMNP06]).
Given a ℚ−\mathbbm{Q}-divisor DD, let 𝔹⁡(D):=⋂k≥1Bs⁡(k​D)\mathbbm{B}(D):=\bigcap_{k\geq 1}\mathrm{Bs}(kD) be the stable base locus of DD where Bs⁡(k​D)\mathrm{Bs}(kD) is the base locus of the linear system |k​D||kD|. The base loci 𝔹+​(D):=⋂A𝔹⁡(D−A)\mathbbm{B}_{+}(D):=\bigcap_{A}\mathbbm{B}(D-A) and 𝔹−​(D):=⋃A𝔹⁡(D+A)\mathbbm{B}_{-}(D):=\bigcup_{A}\mathbbm{B}(D+A), where AA varies among all ample ℚ−\mathbbm{Q}-divisors, are called respectively augmented and restricted base locus of DD. They are invariant under rescaling and 𝔹−​(D)⊂𝔹⁡(D)⊂𝔹+​(D)\mathbbm{B}_{-}(D)\subset\mathbbm{B}(D)\subset\mathbbm{B}_{+}(D). Moreover as described in a work of Nakamaye, [Nak03], the restricted and the augmented base loci are numerical invariants and can be extended to the Neron-Severi space (for a real class it is enough to consider only ample ℝ−\mathbbm{R}-divisors AA such that D±AD\pm A is a ℚ−\mathbbm{Q}-divisor). The stable base loci do not, see Example 1.1.1.1. in [ELMNP06], although by Proposition 1.2.6.1.2.6. in [ELMNP06] the subset where the augmented and restricted base loci are equal is open and dense in the Neron-Severi space N1​(X)ℝ\mathrm{N}^{1}(X)_{\mathbbm{R}}.
Thanks to the numerical invariance of the restricted and augmented base loci, we will often talk of restricted and/or augmented base loci of a ℝ−\mathbbm{R}-line bundle LL. Moreover the restricted base locus can be thought as a measure of the nefness since DD is nef iff 𝔹−​(D)=∅\mathbbm{B}_{-}(D)=\emptyset, while the augmented base locus can be thought as a measure of the ampleness since DD is ample iff 𝔹+​(D)=∅\mathbbm{B}_{+}(D)=\emptyset. Moreover 𝔹−​(D)=X\mathbbm{B}_{-}(D)=X iff DD is not pseudoeffective while 𝔹+​(D)=X\mathbbm{B}_{+}(D)=X iff DD is not big.

2.3 Additive Semigroups and their Okounkov bodies

We briefly recall some notions about the theory of the Okounkov bodies constructed from additive semigroups (the main references are [KKh12] and [Bou14], see also [Kho93]).
Let S⊂ℤn+1S\subset\mathbbm{Z}^{n+1} be an additive subsemigroup not necessarily finitely generated. We denote by C⁡(S)C(S) the closed cone in ℝn+1\mathbbm{R}^{n+1} generated by SS, i.e. the closure of the set of all linear combinations ∑iλi​si\sum_{i}\lambda_{i}s_{i} with λi∈ℝ≥0\lambda_{i}\in\mathbbm{R}_{\geq 0} and si∈Ss_{i}\in S. In this paper we will exclusively work with semigroups SS such that the pair (S,ℝn×ℝ≥0)(S,\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}_{\geq 0}) is admissible, i.e. S⊂ℝn×ℝ≥0S\subset\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}_{\geq 0}, or strongly admissible, i.e. it is admissible and C⁡(S)C(S) intersects the hyperplane ℝn×{0}\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\{0\} only in the origin (see section §​1.2\lx@sectionsign 1.2 in [KKh12]). We recall that a closed convex cone CC with apex the origin is called strictly convex iff the biggest linear subspace contained in CC is the origin, so if (S,ℝn×ℝ≥0)(S,\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}_{\geq 0}) is strongly admissible then C⁡(S)C(S) is strictly convex.

Definition 2.1.

Let (S,ℝn×ℝ≥0)(S,\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}_{\geq 0}) be an admissible pair. Then

Δ⁡(S):=π⁡(C⁡(S)∩{ℝn×{1}})\Delta(S):=\pi\big(C(S)\cap\{\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\{1\}\}\big)

is called Okounkov convex set of (𝐒,ℝ𝐧×ℝ≥𝟎)(\mathbf{S},\mathbbm{R}^{\mathbf{n}}\times\mathbbm{R}_{\mathbf{\geq 0}}), where π:ℝn+1→ℝn\pi:\mathbbm{R}^{n+1}\to\mathbbm{R}^{n} is the projection to the first nn coordinates. If (S,ℝn×ℝ≥0)(S,\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}_{\geq 0}) is strongly admissible, Δ⁡(S)\Delta(S) is also called Okounkov body of (𝐒,ℝ𝐧×ℝ≥𝟎)(\mathbf{S},\mathbbm{R}^{\mathbf{n}}\times\mathbbm{R}_{\mathbf{\geq 0}}).

Remark 2.2.

The convexity of Δ⁡(S)\Delta(S) is immediate, while it is not hard to check that it is compact iff the pair is strongly admissible. Moreover SS generates a subgroup of ℤn+1\mathbbm{Z}^{n+1} of maximal rank iff Δ⁡(S)\Delta(S) has interior not-empty.

The following result is well-known and it has many interesting consequences.

Theorem 2.3 ([KKh12], Theorem 1.4).

Let S⊂ℤn+1S\subset\mathbbm{Z}^{n+1} be a finitely generated subsemigroup. Then there exists an element α0∈S\alpha_{0}\in S such that

α0+C⁡(S)∩G⁡(S)⊂S\alpha_{0}+C(S)\cap G(S)\subset S

where G⁡(S)⊂ℤn+1G(S)\subset\mathbbm{Z}^{n+1} is the group generated by SS.

Defining Sk:={α:(k​α,k)∈S}⊂ℝnS^{k}:=\{\alpha\,:\,(k\alpha,k)\in S\}\subset\mathbbm{R}^{n} for k∈ℕk\in\mathbbm{N}, we get

Proposition 2.4 ([WN15]).

Let (S,ℝn×ℝ≥0)(S,\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}_{\geq 0}) be an admissible pair. Then

Δ⁡(S)=⋃k≥1Sk¯.\Delta(S)=\overline{\bigcup_{k\geq 1}S^{k}}.

Moreover if K⊂Δ​(S)∘⊂ℝnK\subset\Delta(S)^{\circ}\subset\mathbbm{R}^{n} compact subset then K⊂Conv⁡(Sk)K\subset\mathrm{Conv}(S^{k}) for k≥1k\geq 1 divisible enough, where Conv\mathrm{Conv} denotes the closed convex hull. In particular

Δ​(S)∘=⋃k≥1Conv​(Sk)∘=⋃k≥1Conv​(Sk!)∘\Delta(S)^{\circ}=\bigcup_{k\geq 1}\mathrm{Conv}(S^{k})^{\circ}=\bigcup_{k\geq 1}\mathrm{Conv}(S^{k!})^{\circ}

with Conv⁡(Sk!)\mathrm{Conv}(S^{k!}) non-decreasing in kk.

Proof.

The inclusion Δ⁡(S)⊃⋃k≥1Sk¯\Delta(S)\supset\overline{\bigcup_{k\geq 1}S^{k}} is immediate.
To prove the reverse inequality and the rest of the statement we can assume SS finitely generated. Indeed for any SS not finitely generated, Δ⁡(S)\Delta(S) can be approximated by Okounkov convex sets Δ⁡(Sm)\Delta(S_{m}) of an increasing sequence {Sm}m≥1\{S_{m}\}_{m\geq 1} of finitely generated subsemigroups of SS. Clearly Δ⁡(Sm)⊂Δ⁡(Sm+1)⊂⋯⊂Δ⁡(S)\Delta(S_{m})\subset\Delta(S_{m+1})\subset\cdots\subset\Delta(S) and

⋃m≥1Δ⁡(Sm)¯=Δ⁡(S).\overline{\bigcup_{m\geq 1}\Delta(S_{m})}=\Delta(S).

Thus, assuming SS finitely generated and letting α0∈S\alpha_{0}\in S given by Theorem 2.3, (k​α,k)−α0∈C⁡(S)∩G⁡(S)(k\alpha,k)-\alpha_{0}\in C(S)\cap G(S) for any α∈Δ⁡(S)∩(1k​ℤ)n\alpha\in\Delta(S)\cap\big(\frac{1}{k}\mathbbm{Z}\big)^{n} such that (α,1)(\alpha,1) has distance bigger than |α0|/k|\alpha_{0}|/k from the boundary of C⁡(S)C(S). Therefore by Theorem 2.3 (k​α,k)∈S(k\alpha,k)\in S, i.e. α∈Sk\alpha\in S^{k}, which yields Δ⁡(S)⊂⋃k≥1Sk¯\Delta(S)\subset\overline{\bigcup_{k\geq 1}S^{k}} varying α\alpha and k∈ℕk\in\mathbbm{N}. Moreover, for K⊂Δ​(S)∘K\subset\Delta(S)^{\circ} compact subset, letting k0∈ℕk_{0}\in\mathbbm{N} such that |α0|/k0<d⁡(K,∂Δ⁡(S))/2|\alpha_{0}|/k_{0}<d\big(K,\partial\Delta(S)\big)/2, we get K⊂Conv​(Sk)∘K\subset\mathrm{Conv}(S^{k})^{\circ} for any k≥k0k\geq k_{0}. The Proposition follows. ∎

When a strong admissible pair (S,ℝn×ℝ≥0)(S,\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}_{\geq 0}) satisfies the further hypothesis Δ⁡(S)⊂ℝ≥0n\Delta(S)\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}_{\geq 0} then we denote with

Δ​(S)ess:=⋃k≥1Conv​(Sk)ess\Delta(S)^{\mathrm{ess}}:=\bigcup_{k\geq 1}\mathrm{Conv}(S^{k})^{\mathrm{ess}}

the essential Okounkov body where Conv​(Sk)e​s​s\mathrm{Conv}(S^{k})^{ess} represents the interior of Conv⁡(Sk)\mathrm{Conv}(S^{k}) as subset of ℝ≥0n\mathbbm{R}^{n}_{\geq 0} with its induced topology ([WN15]). Note that if SS is finitely generated then Δ​(S)ess\Delta(S)^{\mathrm{ess}} coincides with the interior of Δ⁡(S)\Delta(S) as subset of ℝ≥0n\mathbbm{R}^{n}_{\geq 0}, but in general they may be different since points in the hyperplanes {xi=0}\{x_{i}=0\} may belong to Δ⁡(S)\Delta(S), and hence in its interior as subset of ℝ≥0n\mathbbm{R}^{n}_{\geq 0}, but not in Δ​(S)e​s​s\Delta(S)^{ess}.

Proposition 2.5.

Let (S,ℝn×ℝ≥0)(S,\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}_{\geq 0}) be a strongly admissible pair such that Δ⁡(S)⊂ℝ≥0n\Delta(S)\subset\mathbbm{R}^{n}_{\geq 0}, and let K⊂Δ​(S)essK\subset\Delta(S)^{\mathrm{ess}} be a compact set. Then there exists k≫1k\gg 1 divisible enough such that K⊂Conv​(Sk)essK\subset\mathrm{Conv}(S^{k})^{\mathrm{ess}}. In particular

Δ​(S)ess=⋃k≥1Conv​(Sk!)ess\Delta(S)^{\mathrm{ess}}=\bigcup_{k\geq 1}\mathrm{Conv}(S^{k!})^{\mathrm{ess}}

with Conv​(Sk!)ess\mathrm{Conv}(S^{k!})^{\mathrm{ess}} non-decreasing in kk, and Δ​(S)ess\Delta(S)^{\mathrm{ess}} is an open convex set of ℝ≥0n\mathbbm{R}^{n}_{\geq 0}.

Proof.

We may assume that Δ​(S)ess≠0\Delta(S)^{\mathrm{ess}}\neq 0 otherwise it is trivial. Therefore the subgroup of ℤn+1\mathbbm{Z}^{n+1} generated by SS has maximal rank. Then the proof coincides with that of Proposition 2.4 exploiting again the strength of Theorem 2.3. Indeed the unique difference is that KK may intersect the boundary of Δ⁡(S)\Delta(S) on some hyperplanes {xi=0}\{x_{i}=0\} where with obvious notations (x1,…,xn)(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}) denotes coordinates on ℝ≥0n\mathbbm{R}^{n}_{\geq 0}. But by definition this can only happen if such intersection points belong to Conv​(Sk)e​s​s\mathrm{Conv}(S^{k})^{ess} for some kk. ∎

We also recall the following key Theorem:

Theorem 2.6 ([Bou14], Théorème 1.12.; [KKh12], Theorem 1.14.).

Let (S,ℝn×ℝ≥0)(S,\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}_{\geq 0}) be a strongly admissible pair, let G⁡(S)⊂ℤn+1G(S)\subset\mathbbm{Z}^{n+1} be the group generated by SS and let ind1\mathrm{ind}_{1} and ind2\mathrm{ind}_{2} be respectively the index of the subgroups π1​(G​(S))\pi_{1}\big(G(S)\big) and π2​(G​(S))\pi_{2}\big(G(S)\big) in ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} and in ℤ\mathbbm{Z} where π1\pi_{1} and π2\pi_{2} are respectively the projection to the first nn-coordinates and to the last coordinate. Then

Volℝn​(Δ​(S))ind1​ind2n=limm→∞,m∈ℕ⁡(S)#​Smmn\frac{\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathbbm{R}^{n}}\big(\Delta(S)\big)}{\mathrm{ind}_{1}\mathrm{ind}_{2}^{n}}=\lim_{m\to\infty,m\in\mathbbm{N}(S)}\frac{\#S^{m}}{m^{n}}

where ℕ⁡(S):={m∈ℕ:Sm≠∅}\mathbbm{N}(S):=\{m\in\mathbbm{N}\,:\,S^{m}\neq\emptyset\} and the volume is respect to the Lebesgue measure.

Finally we need to introduce the valuations:

Definition 2.7.

Let VV be an algebra over ℂ\mathbbm{C}. A valuation from VV to ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} equipped with a total additive order >> is a map ν:V∖{0}→(ℤn,>)\nu:V\setminus\{0\}\to(\mathbbm{Z}^{n},>) such that

  • i)

    ν⁡(f+g)≥min⁡{ν⁡(f),ν⁡(g)}\nu(f+g)\geq\min\{\nu(f),\nu(g)\} for any f,g∈V∖{0}f,g\in V\setminus\{0\} such that f+g≠0f+g\neq 0;

  • ii)

    ν⁡(λ​f)=ν⁡(f)\nu(\lambda f)=\nu(f) for any f∈V∖{0}f\in V\setminus\{0\} and any ℂ∋λ≠0\mathbbm{C}\ni\lambda\neq 0;

  • iii)

    ν⁡(f​g)=ν⁡(f)+ν⁡(g)\nu(fg)=\nu(f)+\nu(g) for any f,g∈V∖{0}f,g\in V\setminus\{0\}.

Often ν\nu is defined on the whole VV adding +∞+\infty to the group ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} and imposing ν⁡(0):=+∞\nu(0):=+\infty.
For any α∈ℤn\alpha\in\mathbbm{Z}^{n} the α−\alpha-leaf of the valuation is defined as the quotient of vector spaces

V^α:={f∈V∖{0}:ν⁡(f)≥α}∪{0}{f∈V∖{0}:ν⁡(f)>α}∪{0}.\hat{V}_{\alpha}:=\frac{\{f\in V\setminus\{0\}\,:\,\nu(f)\geq\alpha\}\cup\{0\}}{\{f\in V\setminus\{0\}\,:\,\nu(f)>\alpha\}\cup\{0\}}.

A valuation is said to have one-dimensional leaves if the dimension of any leaf is at most 11.

Proposition 2.8 ([KKh12], Proposition 2.6.).

Let VV be an algebra over ℂ\mathbbm{C}, and let ν:V∖{0}→(ℤn,>)\nu:V\setminus\{0\}\to(\mathbbm{Z}^{n},>) be a valuation with one-dimensional leaves. Then for any no trivial subspaces W⊂VW\subset V,

#​ν​(W∖{0})=dimℂW.\#\nu(W\setminus\{0\})=\dim_{\mathbbm{C}}W.

We will say that a valuation ν:V∖{0}→(ℤn,>)\nu:V\setminus\{0\}\to(\mathbbm{Z}^{n},>) is faithful if the field of fractions KK of VV has transcendental degree nn and the extension ν:K∖{0}→(ℤn,>)\nu:K\setminus\{0\}\to(\mathbbm{Z}^{n},>) defined as ν⁡(f/g):=ν⁡(f)−ν⁡(g)\nu(f/g):=\nu(f)-\nu(g) (see Lemme 2.32.3 in [Bou14]) has the whole ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} as image. Note that any faithful valuation has one-dimensional leaves (see Remark 2.26.2.26. in [Bou14]).

2.4 The Okounkov body associated to a line bundle

In this section we recall the construction and some known results of the Okounkov body associated to a line bundle LL and a point p∈Xp\in X (see [LM09],[KKh12] and [Bou14]).
Consider the abelian group ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} equipped with a total additive order >>, let ν:ℂ⁡(X)∖{0}→(ℤn,>)\nu:\mathbbm{C}(X)\setminus\{0\}\to(\mathbbm{Z}^{n},>) be a faithful valuation with center p∈Xp\in X. We recall that p∈Xp\in X is the (unique) center of ν\nu if 𝒪X,p⊂{f∈ℂ⁡(X):ν⁡(f)≥0}\mathcal{O}_{X,p}\subset\{f\in\mathbbm{C}(X)\,:\,\nu(f)\geq 0\} and 𝔪X,p⊂{f∈ℂ⁡(X):ν⁡(f)>0}\mathfrak{m}_{X,p}\subset\{f\in\mathbbm{C}(X)\,:\,\nu(f)>0\}, and that the semigroup ν⁡(𝒪X,p∖{0})\nu(\mathcal{O}_{X,p}\setminus\{0\}) is well-ordered by the induced order (see §​2\lx@sectionsign 2 in [Bou14]).
Assume that L|UL_{|U} is trivialized by a non–zero local section tt. Then any section s∈H0​(X,k​L)s\in H^{0}(X,kL) can be written locally as s=f​tks=ft^{k} with f∈𝒪X​(U)f\in\mathcal{O}_{X}(U). Thus we define ν⁡(s):=ν⁡(f)\nu(s):=\nu(f), where we identify ℂ⁡(X)\mathbbm{C}(X) with the meromorphic function field and 𝒪X,p\mathcal{O}_{X,p} with the stalk of 𝒪X\mathcal{O}_{X} at pp. We observe that ν⁡(s)\nu(s) does not depend on the trivialization tt chosen since any other trivialization t′t^{\prime} of L|VL_{|V} differs from tt on U∩VU\cap V by an unit u∈𝒪X​(U∩V)u\in\mathcal{O}_{X}(U\cap V). We define an additive semigroup associated to the valuation by

Γ:={(ν(s),k):s∈H0(X,kL)∖{0},k≥1}⊂ℤn×ℤ.\Gamma:=\{(\nu(s),k)\,:\,s\in H^{0}(X,kL)\setminus\{0\},k\geq 1\}\subset\mathbbm{Z}^{n}\times\mathbbm{Z}.

The Okounkov body Δ⁡(L)\Delta(L) is the Okounkov convex set of (Γ,ℝn×ℝ≥0)(\Gamma,\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}_{\geq 0}) (see Definition 2.1), i.e.

Δ⁡(L):=π⁡(C⁡(Γ)∩{ℝn×{1}})\Delta(L):=\pi\big(C(\Gamma)\cap\{\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\{1\}\}\big)

where π:ℝn×ℝ→ℝn\pi:\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}\to\mathbbm{R}^{n} is the projection to the first nn coordinated. By Proposition 2.4 it follows that

Δ(L)=⋃k≥1{ν⁡(s)k:s∈H0​(X,k​L)∖{0}}¯=Conv({ν⁡(s)k:s∈H0(X,kL)∖{0},k≥1}),\Delta(L)=\overline{\bigcup_{k\geq 1}\Big\{\frac{\nu(s)}{k}\,:\,s\in H^{0}(X,kL)\setminus\{0\}\Big\}}=\mathrm{Conv}\Big(\Big\{\frac{\nu(s)}{k}\,:\,s\in H^{0}(X,kL)\setminus\{0\},k\geq 1\Big\}\Big),

and by construction Δ⁡(L)\Delta(L) is a convex set of ℝn\mathbbm{R}^{n} with interior not-empty iff Γ\Gamma generates a subgroup of ℤn+1\mathbbm{Z}^{n+1} of maximal rank (Remark 2.2).
For a prime divisor D∈Div⁡(X)D\in\mathrm{Div}(X) we set ν⁡(D)=ν⁡(f)\nu(D)=\nu(f) for ff any local equation for DD near pp, noting that the map ν:Div⁡(X)→ℤn\nu:\mathrm{Div}(X)\to\mathbbm{Z}^{n} extends to a ℝ−\mathbbm{R}-linear map from Div​(X)ℝ\mathrm{Div}(X)_{\mathbbm{R}}.

Theorem 2.9 ([LM09],[KKh12]).

The following statements hold:

  • i)

    Δ⁡(L)\Delta(L) is a compact convex set lying in ℝn\mathbbm{R}^{n};

  • ii)

    n!​Volℝn​(Δ⁡(L))=VolX​(L)n!\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathbbm{R}^{n}}\big(\Delta(L)\big)=\mathrm{Vol}_{X}(L), and in particular LL is big iff Δ​(L)∘≠∅\Delta(L)^{\circ}\neq\emptyset, i.e Δ⁡(L)\Delta(L) is a convex body;

  • iii)

    if LL is big then Δ(L)={D∈Div≥0(X)ℝ:D≡n​u​mL}¯\Delta(L)=\overline{\{D\in\mathrm{Div}_{\geq 0}(X)_{\mathbbm{R}}\,:\,D\equiv_{num}L\}} and, in particular, the Okounkov body only depends on the numerical class of the big line bundle.

Quasi-monomial valuation

Equip ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} of a total additive order >>, fix λ→1,…,λ→n∈ℤn\vec{\lambda}_{1},\dots,\vec{\lambda}_{n}\in\mathbbm{Z}^{n} linearly independent and fix local holomorphic coordinates {z1,…,zn}\{z_{1},\dots,z_{n}\} around a fixed point pp. Then we can define the quasi-monomial valuation ν:𝒪X,p∖{0}→ℤn\nu:\mathcal{O}_{X,p}\setminus\{0\}\to\mathbbm{Z}^{n} by

ν(f):=min{∑i=1nαiλ→i:aα≠0wherelocallyaroundp,f=U∑α∈ℕnaαzα}\nu(f):=\min\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\alpha_{i}\vec{\lambda}_{i}\,:\,a_{\alpha}\neq 0\,\mathrm{where}\,\mathrm{locally}\,\mathrm{around}\,p,f=_{U}\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbbm{N}^{n}}a_{\alpha}z^{\alpha}\Big\}

where the minimum is taken respect to the order >> fixed on ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n}. Note that such valuation is faithful iff det(λ→1,…,λ→n)=±1\det(\vec{\lambda}_{1},\dots,\vec{\lambda}_{n})=\pm 1.
For instance if we equip ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} of the lexicographical order, for λ→j=e→j\vec{\lambda}_{j}=\vec{e}_{j} (j−j-th vector of the canonical base of ℝn\mathbbm{R}^{n}) we get

ν(f):=minl​e​x{α:aα≠0wherelocallyaroundp,f=U∑α∈ℕnaαzα}.\nu(f):=\min_{lex}\Big\{\alpha\,:\,a_{\alpha}\neq 0\,\mathrm{where}\,\mathrm{locally}\,\mathrm{around}\,p,f=_{U}\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbbm{N}^{n}}a_{\alpha}z^{\alpha}\Big\}.

This is the valuation associated to an admissible flag X=Y0⊃Y1⊃⋯⊃Yn={p}X=Y_{0}\supset Y_{1}\supset\cdots\supset Y_{n}=\{p\}, in the sense of [LM09]44 4 YiY_{i} smooth irreducible subvariety of XX of codimension ii such that YiY_{i} is a Cartier divisor in Yi−1Y_{i-1} for any i=1,…,ni=1,\dots,n., such that locally Yi:={z1=⋯=zi=0}Y_{i}:=\{z_{1}=\cdots=z_{i}=0\} (see also [WN15]).
A change of coordinates with the same local flag produces the same valuation, i.e. the valuation depends uniquely on the local flag.
Note: In the paper a valuation associated to an admissible flag Y⋅Y_{\cdot} will be the valuation constructed by the local procedure starting from local holomorphic coordinates as just described.
On the other hand if we equip ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} of the deglex order and we take λ→i=e→i\vec{\lambda}_{i}=\vec{e}_{i}, we get the valuation ν:𝒪X,p∖{0}→ℤn\nu:\mathcal{O}_{X,p}\setminus\{0\}\to\mathbbm{Z}^{n},

ν(f):=mind​e​g​l​e​x{α:aα≠0wherelocallyaroundp,f=U∑α∈ℕnaαzα}.\nu(f):=\min_{deglex}\Big\{\alpha\,:\,a_{\alpha}\neq 0\,\mathrm{where}\,\mathrm{locally}\,\mathrm{around}\,p,f=_{U}\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbbm{N}^{n}}a_{\alpha}z^{\alpha}\Big\}.

This is the valuation associated to an infinitesimal flag Y⋅Y_{\cdot} in pp: given a flag of subspaces Tp​X=:V0⊃V1⊃⋯⊃Vn={0}T_{p}X=:V_{0}\supset V_{1}\supset\cdots\supset V_{n}=\{0\} such that dimℂVi=n−i\dim_{\mathbbm{C}}V_{i}=n-i, consider on X~:=Blp​X\tilde{X}:=\mathrm{Bl}_{p}X the flag

X~=:Y0⊃ℙ⁡(Tp​X)=ℙ⁡(V0)=:Y1⊃⋯⊃ℙ⁡(Vn−1)=:Yn=:{p~}.\tilde{X}=:Y_{0}\supset\mathbbm{P}(T_{p}X)=\mathbbm{P}(V_{0})=:Y_{1}\supset\cdots\supset\mathbbm{P}(V_{n-1})=:Y_{n}=:\{\tilde{p}\}.

Note that Y⋅Y_{\cdot} is an admissible flag around p~\tilde{p} on the blow-up X~\tilde{X}. Indeed we recover the valuation on X~\tilde{X} associated to this admissible flag considering F∘νF\circ\nu where F:(ℤn,>d​e​g​l​e​x)→(ℤn,>l​e​x)F:(\mathbbm{Z}^{n},>_{deglex})\to(\mathbbm{Z}^{n},>_{lex}) is the order-preserving isomorphism F⁡(α):=(|α|,α1,…,αn−1)F(\alpha):=(|\alpha|,\alpha_{1},\dots,\alpha_{n-1}), i.e. considering the quasi-monomial valuation given by the lexicographical order and λ→i:=e→1+e→i\vec{\lambda}_{i}:=\vec{e}_{1}+\vec{e}_{i}.
Note: In the paper a valuation associated to an infinitesimal flag Y⋅Y_{\cdot} will be the valuation ν\nu constructed by the local procedure starting from local holomorphic coordinates as just described, and in particular the total additive order on ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} will be the deglex order in this case.

2.5 A moment map associated to an (S1)n−(S^{1})^{n}-action on a particular manifold

In this brief subsection we recall some results regarding a moment map for an (S1)n−(S^{1})^{n}-action on a symplectic manifold (M,ω)(M,\omega) constructed from a convex hull of a finite set 𝒜⊂ℕn\mathcal{A}\subset\mathbbm{N}^{n} (see section §​3\lx@sectionsign 3 in [WN15]).

Let 𝒜⊂ℕn\mathcal{A}\subset\mathbbm{N}^{n} be a finite set, let μ:ℂn→ℝn\mu:\mathbbm{C}^{n}\to\mathbbm{R}^{n} be the map μ⁡(z1,…,zn):=(|z1|2,…,|zn|2)\mu(z_{1},\dots,z_{n}):=(|z_{1}|^{2},\dots,|z_{n}|^{2}).
Then if Conv​(𝒜)ess≠∅\mathrm{Conv}(\mathcal{A})^{\mathrm{ess}}\neq\emptyset, we define

𝒟𝒜:=μ−1​(Conv​(𝒜)ess)=μ−1​(Conv⁡(𝒜))∘\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{A}}:=\mu^{-1}\big(\mathrm{Conv}(\mathcal{A})^{\mathrm{ess}}\big)=\mu^{-1}\big(\mathrm{Conv}(\mathcal{A})\big)^{\circ}

where we have denoted by Conv​(𝒜)ess\mathrm{Conv}(\mathcal{A})^{\mathrm{ess}} the interior of Conv⁡(𝒜)\mathrm{Conv}(\mathcal{A}) respect to the induced topology on ℝ≥0n\mathbbm{R}^{n}_{\geq 0}. Next we define M𝒜M_{\mathcal{A}} as the manifold we get removing from ℂn\mathbbm{C}^{n} all submanifolds given by {zi1=⋯=zir=0}\{z_{i_{1}}=\cdots=z_{i_{r}}=0\} which do not intersect 𝒟𝒜\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{A}}. We equip such manifold with the form ω𝒜:=d​dc​ϕ𝒜\omega_{\mathcal{A}}:=dd^{c}\phi_{\mathcal{A}} where

ϕ𝒜​(z):=ln⁡(∑α∈𝒜|𝐳α|2).\phi_{\mathcal{A}}(z):=\ln\Big(\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal{A}}|\mathbf{z}^{\alpha}|^{2}\Big).

Here 𝐳={z1,…,zn}\mathbf{z}=\{z_{1},\dots,z_{n}\} and 𝐳α=z1α1⋯znαn\mathbf{z}^{\alpha}=z_{1}^{\alpha_{1}}\cdots z_{n}^{\alpha_{n}}. Clearly, by construction, ω𝒜\omega_{\mathcal{A}} is an (S1)n−(S^{1})^{n}-invariant Kähler form on M𝒜M_{\mathcal{A}}, so in particular (M𝒜,ω𝒜)(M_{\mathcal{A}},\omega_{\mathcal{A}}) can be thought as a symplectic manifold. Moreover defining f⁡(w1,…,wn):=(ew1/2,…,ewn/2)f(w_{1},\dots,w_{n}):=(e^{w_{1}/2},\dots,e^{w_{n}/2}), the function u𝒜​(w):=ϕ𝒜∘f⁡(w)u_{\mathcal{A}}(w):=\phi_{\mathcal{A}}\circ f(w) is plurisubharmonic and independent of the imaginary part yiy_{i}, and f∗​ω𝒜=d​dc​u𝒜f^{*}\omega_{\mathcal{A}}=dd^{c}u_{\mathcal{A}}. Thus an easy calculation shows that

d​dc​u𝒜=14​π​∑j,k=1n∂2u𝒜∂xk​∂xj​d​yk∧d​xjdd^{c}u_{\mathcal{A}}=\frac{1}{4\pi}\sum_{j,k=1}^{n}\frac{\partial^{2}u_{\mathcal{A}}}{\partial x_{k}\partial x_{j}}dy_{k}\wedge dx_{j}

which implies

d​∂∂xk​u𝒜=d​dc​u𝒜​(4​π​∂∂yk,⋅).d\frac{\partial}{\partial x_{k}}u_{\mathcal{A}}=dd^{c}u_{\mathcal{A}}\Big(4\pi\frac{\partial}{\partial y_{k}},\cdot\Big).

Therefore, setting Hk:=∂u𝒜∂xk∘f−1H_{k}:=\frac{\partial u_{\mathcal{A}}}{\partial x_{k}}\circ f^{-1}, since (f−1)∗​(2​π​∂∂θk)=4​π​∂∂yk(f^{-1})_{*}\big(2\pi\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta_{k}}\big)=4\pi\frac{\partial}{\partial y_{k}}, we get

d​Hk=ω𝒜​(2​π​∂∂θk,⋅).dH_{k}=\omega_{\mathcal{A}}\Big(2\pi\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta_{k}},\cdot\Big).

Hence μ𝒜=(H1,…,Hn)=∇u𝒜∘f−1\mu_{\mathcal{A}}=(H_{1},\dots,H_{n})=\nabla u_{\mathcal{A}}\circ f^{-1} is a moment map for the (S1)n−(S^{1})^{n}-action on the symplectic manifold (M𝒜,ω𝒜)(M_{\mathcal{A}},\omega_{\mathcal{A}}). Furthermore it is not hard to check that μ𝒜​((ℂ∗)n)=Conv​(𝒜)∘\mu_{\mathcal{A}}\big((\mathbbm{C}^{*})^{n}\big)=\mathrm{Conv}(\mathcal{A})^{\circ}, that μ𝒜​(M𝒜)=Conv​(𝒜)ess\mu_{\mathcal{A}}(M_{\mathcal{A}})=\mathrm{Conv}(\mathcal{A})^{\mathrm{ess}} and that for any U⊂M𝒜U\subset M_{\mathcal{A}}, setting f−1​(U)=V×(i​ℝn)f^{-1}(U)=V\times(i\mathbbm{R}^{n}),

∫Uω𝒜n=∫V×(i⁡[0,4​π])n(d​dc​u𝒜)n=n!​∫Vdet(Hess⁡(u𝒜))=n!​∫∇u𝒜​(V)𝑑x=n!​Vol​(μ𝒜​(U)).\int_{U}\omega_{\mathcal{A}}^{n}=\int_{V\times(i[0,4\pi])^{n}}(dd^{c}u_{\mathcal{A}})^{n}=n!\int_{V}\det(\mathrm{Hess}(u_{\mathcal{A}}))=n!\int_{\nabla u_{\mathcal{A}}(V)}dx=n!\mathrm{Vol}(\mu_{\mathcal{A}}(U)).

Finally we quote here an useful result:

Lemma 2.10 ([WN15], Lemma 3.1.3.1.).

Let UU be a relatively compact open subset of 𝒟𝒜\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{A}}. Then there exists a smooth function g:MA→ℝg:M_{A}\to\mathbbm{R} with compact support such that ω=ω𝒜+d​dc​g\omega=\omega_{\mathcal{A}}+dd^{c}g is Kähler and ω=ωs​t\omega=\omega_{st} over UU.

3 Multipoint Okounkov bodies

We fix an additive total order >> on ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} and a family of faithful valuations νpj:ℂ⁡(X)∖{0}→(ℤn,>)\nu^{p_{j}}:\mathbbm{C}(X)\setminus\{0\}\to(\mathbbm{Z}^{n},>) centered at pjp_{j}, where recall that p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} are different points chosen on the n−n-dimensional projective manifold XX and LL is a line bundle on XX.

Definition 3.1.

We define V⋅,j⊂R⁡(X,L)V_{\cdot,j}\subset R(X,L) as

Vk,j={s∈H0​(X,k​L)∖{0}:νpj​(s)<νpi​(s)​for​any​i≠j}.V_{k,j}=\{s\in H^{0}(X,kL)\setminus\{0\}\,:\,\nu^{p_{j}}(s)<\nu^{p_{i}}(s)\,\mathrm{for}\,\mathrm{any}\,i\neq j\}.
Remark 3.2.

They are disjoint graded subsemigroups with respect to the multiplicative action since νpj​(s1⊗s2)=νpj​(s1)+νpj​(s2)\nu^{p_{j}}(s_{1}\otimes s_{2})=\nu^{p_{j}}(s_{1})+\nu^{p_{j}}(s_{2}), but they are not necessarily closed under addition and ∪j=1NVk,j\cup_{j=1}^{N}V_{k,j} is typically strictly contained in H0​(X,k​L)∖{0}H^{0}(X,kL)\setminus\{0\} for some k≥1k\geq 1. Note that Vk,jV_{k,j} contains sections whose leading term at pjp_{j} with respect to νpj\nu^{p_{j}} is strictly smaller than the leading term at pip_{i} with respect to νpi\nu^{p_{i}} for any i≠ji\neq j.

Clearly the properties of the valuations νpj\nu^{p_{j}} assure that

  • i)

    νpj​(s)=+∞\nu^{p_{j}}(s)=+\infty iff s=0s=0 (by extension νpj​(0):=+∞\nu^{p_{j}}(0):=+\infty);

  • ii)

    for any s∈V⋅,js\in V_{\cdot,j} and for any 0≠a∈ℂ0\neq a\in\mathbbm{C}, νpj​(a​s)=νpj​(s)\nu^{p_{j}}(as)=\nu^{p_{j}}(s).

Thus we can define

Γj:={(νpj(s),k):s∈Vk,j,k≥1}⊂ℤn×ℤ.\Gamma_{j}:=\{(\nu^{p_{j}}(s),k)\,:\,s\in V_{k,j},k\geq 1\}\subset\mathbbm{Z}^{n}\times\mathbbm{Z}.
Lemma 3.3.

Γj\Gamma_{j} is an additive subsemigroup of ℤn+1\mathbbm{Z}^{n+1} and (Γj,ℝn×ℝ)(\Gamma_{j},\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}) is a strongly admissible pair.

Proof.

The first part is an immediate consequence of the definition, while the second assertion follows from the inclusion Γj⊂Γpj:={(νpj(s),k):s∈H0(X,kL)∖{0},k≥1}\Gamma_{j}\subset\Gamma_{p_{j}}:=\{(\nu^{p_{j}}(s),k)\,:\,s\in H^{0}(X,kL)\setminus\{0\},k\geq 1\} (see subsection 2.4). ∎

Definition 3.4.

We call Δj​(L):=Δ⁡(Γj)\Delta_{j}(L):=\Delta(\Gamma_{j}) the multipoint Okounkov body of LL at pjp_{j}.

Observe that by Proposition 2.4 Δj​(L)=⋃k≥1νpj​(Vk,j)k¯\Delta_{j}(L)=\overline{\bigcup_{k\geq 1}\frac{\nu^{p_{j}}(V_{k,j})}{k}} and that these multipoint Okounkov bodies depend on the choice of the faithful valuations νp1,…,νpN\nu^{p_{1}},\dots,\nu^{p_{N}}, but we omit the dependence to simplify the notations.

Remark 3.5.

If we fix local holomorphic coordinates {zj,1,…,zj,n}\{z_{j,1},\dots,z_{j,n}\} around pjp_{j}, we can consider any family of faithful quasi-monomial valuations νpj\nu^{p_{j}} with center p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} (see paragraph §​2.4\lx@sectionsign\ref{paragraph:ParticularValuations}) with respect to the same choice of a total additive order on ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} and to the choice of families of ℤ−\mathbbm{Z}-linearly independent vectors λ→1,j,…,λ→n,j∈ℤn\vec{\lambda}_{1,j},\dots,\vec{\lambda}_{n,j}\in\mathbbm{Z}^{n} (these families of vectors may be different). For instance we can choose those associated to the family of admissible flags Yj,i:={zj,1=⋯=zj,i=0}Y_{j,i}:=\{z_{j,1}=\cdots=z_{j,i}=0\} (with ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} equipped of the lexicographical order) or those associated to the family of infinitesimal flags Yj,⋅Y_{j,\cdot} (with in this case ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} equipped pf the deglex order).

Lemma 3.6.

The following statements hold:

  • i)

    Δj​(L)\Delta_{j}(L) is a compact convex set contained in ℝn\mathbbm{R}^{n};

  • ii)

    if pj∉𝔹+​(L)p_{j}\notin\mathbbm{B}_{+}(L) then Γj​(L)\Gamma_{j}(L) generates ℤn+1\mathbbm{Z}^{n+1} as a group. In particular Δj​(L)∘≠∅\Delta_{j}(L)^{\circ}\neq\emptyset;

  • iii)

    if Γj​(L)\Gamma_{j}(L) is not empty then it generates ℤn+1\mathbbm{Z}^{n+1} as a group. In particular Δj​(L)∘≠∅\Delta_{j}(L)^{\circ}\neq\emptyset iff Δj​(L)≠∅\Delta_{j}(L)\neq\emptyset.

Proof.

The first point follows by construction (see Definition 2.1 and Remark 2.2).
Proof of (ii). Proceeding similarly to Lemma 2.22.2 in [LM09], let DD be a big divisor such that L=𝒪X​(D)L=\mathcal{O}_{X}(D) and let A,BA,B be two fixed ample divisors such that D=A−BD=A-B. Since DD is big there exists ℕ∋k≫1\mathbbm{N}\ni k\gg 1 such that k​D−BkD-B is linearly equivalent to an effective divisor FF.
Moreover, since by hypothesis pj∉𝔹+​(L)p_{j}\notin\mathbbm{B}_{+}(L), by taking k≫1k\gg 1 big enough, we may assume that pj∉Supp⁡(F)p_{j}\notin\mathrm{Supp}(F) (see Corollary 1.6.1.6. in [ELMNP06]), thus FF is described by a global section ff that is an unity in 𝒪X,pj\mathcal{O}_{X,p_{j}}. Then, possibly adding a very ample divisor to AA and BB we may suppose that there exist sections s0,…,sn∈V1,j​(B)s_{0},\dots,s_{n}\in V_{1,j}(B) such that νpj​(s0)=0→\nu^{p_{j}}(s_{0})=\vec{0} and νpj​(sl)=λ→l\nu^{p_{j}}(s_{l})=\vec{\lambda}_{l} for any l=1,…,nl=1,\dots,n where λ→1,…,λ→n\vec{\lambda}_{1},\dots,\vec{\lambda}_{n} are linearly independent vectors in ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} which generate all ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} as a group (remember that the valuations νpj\nu^{p_{j}} are faithful). Thus, since si⊗f∈V1,j​(k​L)s_{i}\otimes f\in V_{1,j}(kL) for any i=0,…,ni=0,\dots,n and νpj​(f)=0→\nu^{p_{j}}(f)=\vec{0}, we get

(0→,k),(λ→1,k),…,(λ→n,k)∈Γj​(L).(\vec{0},k),(\vec{\lambda}_{1},k),\dots,(\vec{\lambda}_{n},k)\in\Gamma_{j}(L).

And, since (k+1)​D−F(k+1)D-F is linearly equivalent to AA we may also assume that (0→,k+1)∈Γj​(L)(\vec{0},k+1)\in\Gamma_{j}(L), which concludes the proof of (i​i)(ii).
Proof of (iii). Let s∈Vk,j​(L)s\in V_{k,j}(L) such that (νpj​(s),k)∈Γj​(L)(\nu^{p_{j}}(s),k)\in\Gamma_{j}(L) and set w→:=νpj​(s)\vec{w}:=\nu^{p_{j}}(s). Then by Lemma 2.22.2 in [LM09] there exists m∈ℕm\in\mathbbm{N} big enough and a vector v→∈ℤn\vec{v}\in\mathbbm{Z}^{n} such that

(v→,m),(v→+λ→1,m),…,(v→+λ→n,m),(v→,m+1)∈Γ⁡(L)(\vec{v},m),(\vec{v}+\vec{\lambda}_{1},m),\dots,(\vec{v}+\vec{\lambda}_{n},m),(\vec{v},m+1)\in\Gamma(L) (1)

where with Γ⁡(L)\Gamma(L) we denote the semigroup associated to νpj\nu^{p_{j}} for the one-point Okounkov body (see subsection 2.4) and where λ→1,…,λ→n\vec{\lambda}_{1},\dots,\vec{\lambda}_{n} are linearly independent vectors in ℤn\mathbbm{Z}^{n} as in (i​i)(ii). The points in (1) correspond to sections t0,…,tn∈H0​(X,m​L)∖{0},tn+1∈H0​(X,(m+1)​L)∖{0}t_{0},\dots,t_{n}\in H^{0}(X,mL)\setminus\{0\},t_{n+1}\in H^{0}(X,(m+1)L)\setminus\{0\}. Next by definition of V⋅,j​(L)V_{\cdot,j}(L) there exists N≫1N\gg 1 big enough such that sN⊗tj∈VN​k+m,j​(L)s^{N}\otimes t_{j}\in V_{Nk+m,j}(L) for any j=0,…,nj=0,\dots,n and sN⊗tn+1∈VN​k+m+1​(L)s^{N}\otimes t_{n+1}\in V_{Nk+m+1}(L). Therefore

(N​w→+v→,m),(N​w→+v→+λ→1,m),…,(N​w→+v→+λ→n,k),(N​w→+v→,m+1)∈Γj​(L),(N\vec{w}+\vec{v},m),(N\vec{w}+\vec{v}+\vec{\lambda}_{1},m),\dots,(N\vec{w}+\vec{v}+\vec{\lambda}_{n},k),(N\vec{w}+\vec{v},m+1)\in\Gamma_{j}(L),

which concludes the proof. ∎

Remark 3.7.

Let XX be a curve, LL be a line bundle of degree deg⁡L=c\deg L=c, and p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} be different points on XX. Then by the proof of Lemma 3.6, Δj​(L)\Delta_{j}(L) are intervals in ℝ\mathbbm{R} containing the origin. Moreover if the points are very general and the faithful valuations νpj\nu^{p_{j}} are associated to admissible or to infinitesimal flags, then Δj​(L)=[0,c/N]\Delta_{j}(L)=[0,c/N] for any j=1,…,Nj=1,\dots,N as a consequence of Theorem A.

Remark 3.8.

In higher dimension, however, the situation is more complicated. Indeed it may happen that Δj​(L)=∅\Delta_{j}(L)=\emptyset for some jj as the following simple example shows.
Consider on X=Blq​ℙ2X=\mathrm{Bl}_{q}\mathbbm{P}^{2} two points p1∉Supp⁡(E)p_{1}\notin\mathrm{Supp}(E) and p2∈Supp⁡(E)p_{2}\in\mathrm{Supp}(E) (EE exceptional divisor), and consider the big line bundle L:=H+a​EL:=H+aE for a>1a>1. Clearly, if we consider the family of admissible flags given by any fixed holomorphic coordinates centered at p1p_{1} and holomorphic coordinates {z1,2,z2,2}\{z_{1,2},z_{2,2}\} centered at p2p_{2} where locally E={z1,2=0}E=\{z_{1,2}=0\}, then Δ2​(L)=∅\Delta_{2}(L)=\emptyset. Indeed by the theory of one-point Okounkov bodies for surfaces (see section 6.26.2 in [LM09]) Δ1​(L)⊂Δp1​(L)=Σ\Delta_{1}(L)\subset\Delta^{p_{1}}(L)=\Sigma (where Σ\Sigma is the standard 2−2-simplex and Δp1​(L)\Delta^{p_{1}}(L) the one-point Okounkov body) while Δ2​(L)⊂Δp2​(L)=(a,0)+Σ−1\Delta_{2}(L)\subset\Delta^{p_{2}}(L)=(a,0)+\Sigma^{-1} (Σ−1=C​o​n​v​(0→,e→1,e→1+e→2)\Sigma^{-1}=Conv(\vec{0},\vec{e}_{1},\vec{e}_{1}+\vec{e}_{2}) inverted simplex), and the conclusion follows by construction. Actually, from Theorem A we get Δ1​(L)=Σ\Delta_{1}(L)=\Sigma.
We refer to subsection 6.2 for a detailed analysis on the multipoint Okounkov bodies on surfaces, and to subsection 6.1 for the toric case.

3.1 Proof of Theorem A

The goal of this section is to prove Theorem A.

Theorem A.

Let LL be a big line bundle. Then

n!​∑j=1NVolℝn​(Δj​(L))=VolX​(L)n!\sum_{j=1}^{N}\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathbbm{R}^{n}}(\Delta_{j}(L))=\mathrm{Vol}_{X}(L)

Proposition 3.10.

Let LL be a big line bundle. Proposition 3.10 naturally extends the definition of the multipoint Okounkov bodies to ℚ\mathbbm{Q}-line bundles.
We are now ready to prove Theorem A.

Proof of Theorem A.

By Lemma 3.9 and Theorem 2.6 we get

n!​∑j=1NVolℝn​(ΔjW​(L))ind1,j​(L)​ind2,j​(L)n=limk∈ℕ⁡(L),k→∞n!​∑j=1N#​ΓW,jkkn=limk∈ℕ⁡(L),k→∞h0​(X,k​L)kn/n!=VolX​(L).n!\sum_{j=1}^{N}\frac{\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathbbm{R}^{n}}(\Delta_{j}^{W}(L))}{\mathrm{ind}_{1,j}(L)\mathrm{ind}_{2,j}(L)^{n}}=\lim_{k\in\mathbbm{N}(L),k\to\infty}\frac{n!\sum_{j=1}^{N}\#\Gamma_{W,j}^{k}}{k^{n}}=\lim_{k\in\mathbbm{N}(L),k\to\infty}\frac{h^{0}(X,kL)}{k^{n}/n!}=\mathrm{Vol}_{X}(L). (2)

where we keep the same notations of Theorem 2.6 for the indexes ind1,j​(L),ind2,j​(L)\mathrm{ind}_{1,j}(L),\mathrm{ind}_{2,j}(L) adding the jj subscript to keep track of the points and the dependence on the line bundle since we want to perturb it.
Key point: We claim that

ΔjW​(L)∘=Δj​(L)∘,\Delta_{j}^{W}(L)^{\circ}=\Delta_{j}(L)^{\circ}, (3)

for any j=1,…,N{j=1,\dots,N}. Note that since ΓV,j⊂ΓW,j\Gamma_{V,j}\subset\Gamma_{W,j} we only need to prove that ΔjW​(L)∘⊂Δj​(L)∘\Delta_{j}^{W}(L)^{\circ}\subset\Delta_{j}(L)^{\circ}.
Let AA be a fixed ample line bundle AA such that there exist s1,…,sN∈H0​(X,A){s_{1},\dots,s_{N}\in H^{0}(X,A)} with si∈V1,i​(A)s_{i}\in V_{1,i}(A) and νpi​(si)=0\nu^{p_{i}}(s_{i})=0. Thus we get ΔjW​(m​L−A)⊂Δj​(m​L){\Delta_{j}^{W}(mL-A)\subset\Delta_{j}(mL)} for each m∈ℕm\in\mathbbm{N} and for any j=1,…,Nj=1,\dots,N since s⊗sjk∈Vk,j​(m​L)s\otimes s_{j}^{k}\in V_{k,j}(mL) for any s∈Wk,j​(m​L−A)s\in W_{k,j}(mL-A). Hence

ΔjW​(L−1m​A)⊂Δj​(L)⊂ΔjW​(L)\Delta_{j}^{W}\Big(L-\frac{1}{m}A\Big)\subset\Delta_{j}(L)\subset\Delta_{j}^{W}(L) (4)

by Proposition 3.10.
Moreover since m→ind1,j​(L−1m​A)m\to\mathrm{ind}_{1,j}(L-\frac{1}{m}A) and m→ind2,j​(L−1m​A)m\to\mathrm{ind}_{2,j}(L-\frac{1}{m}A) are decreasing functions, (2) implies

lim supm→∞n!​∑j=1NVolℝn​(ΔjW​(L−1m​A))ind1,j​(L)​ind2,j​(L)n≥lim supm→∞n!​∑j=1NVolℝn​(ΔjW​(L−1m​A))ind1,j​(L−1m​A)​ind2,j​(L−1m​A)n==lim supm→∞VolX​(L−1m​A)=VolX​(L)=n!​∑j=1NVolℝn​(ΔjW​(L))ind1,j​(L)​ind2,j​(L)n\limsup_{m\to\infty}n!\sum_{j=1}^{N}\frac{\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathbbm{R}^{n}}\big(\Delta_{j}^{W}(L-\frac{1}{m}A)\big)}{\mathrm{ind}_{1,j}(L)\mathrm{ind}_{2,j}(L)^{n}}\geq\limsup_{m\to\infty}n!\sum_{j=1}^{N}\frac{\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathbbm{R}^{n}}\big(\Delta_{j}^{W}(L-\frac{1}{m}A)\big)}{\mathrm{ind}_{1,j}(L-\frac{1}{m}A)\mathrm{ind}_{2,j}(L-\frac{1}{m}A)^{n}}=\\ =\limsup_{m\to\infty}\mathrm{Vol}_{X}\Big(L-\frac{1}{m}A\Big)=\mathrm{Vol}_{X}(L)=n!\sum_{j=1}^{N}\frac{\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathbbm{R}^{n}}\big(\Delta_{j}^{W}(L)\big)}{\mathrm{ind}_{1,j}(L)\mathrm{ind}_{2,j}(L)^{n}} (5)

where we used the continuity of the volume function on line bundles. Thus since ΔjW​(L−1m​A)⊂ΔjW​(L−1l​A)\Delta_{j}^{W}(L-\frac{1}{m}A)\subset\Delta_{j}^{W}(L-\frac{1}{l}A) if l>ml>m for any j=1,…,Nj=1,\dots,N, from (5) we deduce that m→Volℝn​(ΔjW​(L−1m​A))m\to\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathbbm{R}^{n}}(\Delta_{j}^{W}(L-\frac{1}{m}A)) is a continuous increasing function converging to Volℝn​(ΔjW​(L))\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathbbm{R}^{n}}(\Delta_{j}^{W}(L)) for any j=1,…,Nj=1,\dots,N. Hence (3) follows from (4).
Conclusion. Finally combining (3) and Lemma 3.6.(ii).(ii) we find out that ind1,j​(L)=ind2,j​(L)=1\mathrm{ind}_{1,j}(L)=\mathrm{ind}_{2,j}(L)=1 if Volℝn​(ΔjW​(L))≠0\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathbbm{R}^{n}}\big(\Delta_{j}^{W}(L)\big)\neq 0. Finally (2) yields

n!​∑j=1NVolℝn​(Δj​(L))=n!​∑j=1NVolℝn​(ΔjW​(L))ind1,j​(L)​ind2,j​(L)n=VolX​(L),n!\sum_{j=1}^{N}\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathbbm{R}^{n}}\big(\Delta_{j}(L)\big)=n!\sum_{j=1}^{N}\frac{\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathbbm{R}^{n}}\big(\Delta_{j}^{W}(L)\big)}{\mathrm{ind}_{1,j}(L)\mathrm{ind}_{2,j}(L)^{n}}=\mathrm{Vol}_{X}(L),

which concludes the proof. ∎

3.2 Variation of multipoint Okounkov bodies

Similarly to the section §​4\lx@sectionsign 4 in [LM09], we prove that for fixed faithful valuations νpj\nu^{p_{j}} centered a NN different points the construction of the multipoint Okounkov Bodies is a numerical invariant, i.e. Δj​(L)\Delta_{j}(L) depends only from the first Chern class c1​(L)∈N1​(X)c_{1}(L)\in\mathrm{N}^{1}(X) of the big line bundle LL, where we have denoted by N1​(X)\mathrm{N}^{1}(X) the Neron-Severi group. Recall that ρ⁡(X):=dimN1​(X)ℝ<∞\rho(X):=\dim\mathrm{N}^{1}(X)_{\mathbbm{R}}<\infty where N1​(X)ℝ:=N1​(X)⊗ℤℝ\mathrm{N}^{1}(X)_{\mathbbm{R}}:=\mathrm{N}^{1}(X)\otimes_{\mathbbm{Z}}\mathbbm{R}.

Proposition 3.11.

Let LL be a big line bundle. Then Δj​(L)\Delta_{j}(L) is a numerical invariant.

Proof.

Assume Δj​(L)∘≠∅\Delta_{j}(L)^{\circ}\neq\emptyset, which by Lemma 3.6 is equivalent to Δj​(L)≠∅\Delta_{j}(L)\neq\emptyset, and let L′L^{\prime} such that L′=L+PL^{\prime}=L+P for PP numerically trivial. Fix also an ample line bundle AA. Then for any m∈ℕm\in\mathbbm{N} there exist km∈ℕk_{m}\in\mathbbm{N} and sm∈H0​(X,km​m​(P+1m​A)){s_{m}\in H^{0}(X,k_{m}m(P+\frac{1}{m}A))} such that sm​(pi)≠0s_{m}(p_{i})\neq 0 for any i=1,…,Ni=1,\dots,N since P+1m​AP+\frac{1}{m}A is a ample ℚ−\mathbbm{Q}-line bundle. Hence we get Δj​(L)⊂Δj​(L′+1m​A)\Delta_{j}(L)\subset\Delta_{j}(L^{\prime}+\frac{1}{m}A) by homogeneity (Proposition 3.10) because s⊗smk∈Vk,j​(km​m​L′+km​A)s\otimes s_{m}^{k}\in V_{k,j}(k_{m}mL^{\prime}+k_{m}A) for any section s∈Vk,j​(km​m​L)s\in V_{k,j}(k_{m}mL). Therefore similarly to the proof of Theorem A, letting m→∞m\to\infty, we obtain Δj​(L)⊂Δj​(L′)\Delta_{j}(L)\subset\Delta_{j}(L^{\prime}). Replacing LL by L+PL+P and PP by −P-P, Lemma 3.6 concludes the proof. ∎

Setting r:=ρ⁡(X)r:=\rho(X) for simplicity, fix L1,…,LrL_{1},\dots,L_{r} line bundles such that {c1​(L1),…,c1​(Lr)}\{c_{1}(L_{1}),\dots,c_{1}(L_{r})\} is a ℤ−\mathbbm{Z-}basis of N1​(X)\mathrm{N}^{1}(X): this lead to natural identifications N1​(X)≃ℤr\mathrm{N}^{1}(X)\simeq\mathbbm{Z}^{r}, N1​(X)ℝ≃ℝr\mathrm{N}^{1}(X)_{\mathbbm{\mathbbm{R}}}\simeq\mathbbm{R}^{r}. Moreover by Lemma 4.6.4.6. in [LM09] we may choose L1,…,LrL_{1},\dots,L_{r} such that the pseudoeffective cone is contained in in the positive orthant of ℝr\mathbbm{R}^{r}.

Definition 3.12.

Letting

Γj(X):=Γj(X;L1,…,Lr):={(νpj(s),m→):s∈Vm→,j(L1,…,Lr))∖{0},m→∈ℕr}⊂ℤn×ℕr\Gamma_{j}(X):=\Gamma_{j}(X;L_{1},\dots,L_{r}):=\{(\nu^{p_{j}}(s),\vec{m})\,:\,s\in V_{\vec{m},j}(L_{1},\dots,L_{r}))\setminus\{0\},\\ \vec{m}\in\mathbbm{N}^{r}\}\subset\mathbbm{Z}^{n}\times\mathbbm{N}^{r}

be the global multipoint semigroup of XX at pjp_{j} with p1,…​pj^,…,pNp_{1},\dots\hat{p_{j}},\dots,p_{N} fixed (it is an addittive subsemigroup of ℤn+r\mathbbm{Z}^{n+r}) where Vm→,j​(L1,…,Lr):={s∈H0​(X,m→⋅(L1,…,Lr))∖{0}:νpj​(s)<νpi​(s)​for​any​i≠j}V_{\vec{m},j}(L_{1},\dots,L_{r}):=\{s\in H^{0}(X,\vec{m}\cdot(L_{1},\dots,L_{r}))\setminus\{0\}\,:\,\nu^{p_{j}}(s)<\nu^{p_{i}}(s)\,\mathrm{for}\,\mathrm{any}\,i\neq j\}, we define

Δj​(X):=C⁡(Γj​(X))\Delta_{j}(X):=C(\Gamma_{j}(X))

as the closed convex cone in ℝn+r\mathbbm{R}^{n+r} generated by Γj​(X)\Gamma_{j}(X), and call it the global multipoint Okounkov body at pjp_{j}.

Lemma 3.13.

The semigroup Γj​(X)\Gamma_{j}(X) generates a subgroup of ℤn+r\mathbbm{Z}^{n+r} of maximal rank.

Proof.

Since the ample cone Amp⁡(X)\mathrm{Amp}(X) is open non-empty set in N1​(X)ℝ\mathrm{N}^{1}(X)_{\mathbbm{R}}, we can fix F1,…,FrF_{1},\dots,F_{r} ample line bundles generating N1​(X)\mathrm{N}^{1}(X) as free ℤ−\mathbbm{Z}-module. Moreover, by the assumptions done for L1,…,LrL_{1},\dots,L_{r} we know that for every i=1,…,ri=1,\dots,r there exists a→i\vec{a}_{i} such that Fi=a→i⋅(L1,…,Lr)F_{i}=\vec{a}_{i}\cdot(L_{1},\dots,L_{r}). Thus, for any i=1,…,ri=1,\dots,r, the graded semigroup Γj​(Fi)\Gamma_{j}(F_{i}) sits in Γj​(X)\Gamma_{j}(X) in a natural way and it generates a subgroup of ℤn×ℤ⋅a→i\mathbbm{Z}^{n}\times\mathbbm{Z}\cdot\vec{a}_{i} of maximal rank by point OPENi​i)ii) in Lemma 3.6 since 𝔹+​(Fi)=∅\mathbbm{B}_{+}(F_{i})=\emptyset. We conclude observing that a→1,…,a→r\vec{a}_{1},\dots,\vec{a}_{r} span ℤr\mathbbm{Z}^{r}. ∎

Next we need a further fact about additive semigroups and their cones. Let Γ⊂ℤn×ℕr\Gamma\subset\mathbbm{Z}^{n}\times\mathbbm{N}^{r} be an additive semigroup, and let C⁡(Γ)⊂ℝn×ℝrC(\Gamma)\subset\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}^{r} be the closed convex cone generated by Γ\Gamma. We call the support of Γ\Gamma respect to the last rr coordinates, Supp⁡(Γ)\mathrm{Supp}(\Gamma), the closed convex cone C⁡(π⁡(Γ))⊂ℝrC(\pi(\Gamma))\subset\mathbbm{R}^{r} where π:ℝn×ℝr→ℝr\pi:\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}^{r}\to\mathbbm{R}^{r} is the usual projection. Then, given a→∈ℕr\vec{a}\in\mathbbm{N}^{r}, we set Γℕ​a→:=Γ∩(ℤn×ℕ​a→)\Gamma_{\mathbbm{N}\vec{a}}:=\Gamma\cap(\mathbbm{Z}^{n}\times\mathbbm{N}\vec{a}) and denote by C⁡(Γℕ​a→)⊂ℝn×ℝ​a→C(\Gamma_{\mathbbm{N}\vec{a}})\subset\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}\vec{a} the closed convex cone generated by Γℕ​a→\Gamma_{\mathbbm{N}\vec{a}} when we consider it as an additive semigroup of ℤn×ℤ​a→≃ℤn+1\mathbbm{Z}^{n}\times\mathbbm{Z}\vec{a}\simeq\mathbbm{Z}^{n+1}.

Proposition 3.14 ([LM09], Proposition 4.9.4.9.).

Assume that Γ\Gamma generates a subgroup of finite index in ℤn×ℤr\mathbbm{Z}^{n}\times\mathbbm{Z}^{r}, and let a→∈ℕr\vec{a}\in\mathbbm{N}^{r} be a vector lying in the interior of Supp⁡(Γ)\mathrm{Supp}(\Gamma). Then

C⁡(Γℕ​a→)=C⁡(Γ)∩(ℝn×ℝ​a→)C(\Gamma_{\mathbbm{N}\vec{a}})=C(\Gamma)\cap(\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}\vec{a})

Now we are ready to prove the main theorem of this section:

Theorem 3.15.

The global multipoint Okounkov body Δj​(X)\Delta_{j}(X) is characterized by the property that in the following diagram

the fiber of Δj​(X)\Delta_{j}(X) over any cohomology class c1​(L)c_{1}(L) of a big ℚ−\mathbbm{Q}-line bundle LL such that c1​(L)∈Supp​(Γj​(X))∘c_{1}(L)\in\mathrm{Supp}(\Gamma_{j}(X))^{\circ} is the multipoint Okounkov body associated to LL at pjp_{j}, i.e Δj​(X)∩pr2−1​(c1​(L))=Δj​(L)\Delta_{j}(X)\cap\mathrm{pr}_{2}^{-1}(c_{1}(L))=\Delta_{j}(L). Moreover Supp(Γj(X))∘∩N1(X)ℚ={c1(L):Δj(L)≠∅,Lℚ−linebundle}\mathrm{Supp}\big(\Gamma_{j}(X)\big)^{\circ}\cap N^{1}(X)_{\mathbbm{Q}}=\{c_{1}(L)\,:\,\Delta_{j}(L)\neq\emptyset,\,L\,\mathbbm{Q}\mathrm{-line}\,\mathrm{bundle}\}.

Remark 3.16.

It is unclear how Supp​(Γj​(X))∘\mathrm{Supp}(\Gamma_{j}(X))^{\circ} can be described. By second point in Lemma 3.6, it contains the open convex set B+​(pj)CB_{+}(p_{j})^{C} where B+​(pj):={α∈N1​(X)ℝ:p∈𝔹+​(α)}B_{+}(p_{j}):=\{\alpha\in\mathrm{N}^{1}(X)_{\mathbbm{R}}\,:\,p\in\mathbbm{B}_{+}(\alpha)\} is closed respect to the metric topology on N1​(X)ℝN^{1}(X)_{\mathbbm{R}} by Proposition 1.2.1.2. in [KL15a] and its complement is convex as easy consequence of Proposition 1.5. in [ELMNP06]. But in general Supp​(Γj​(X))∘\mathrm{Supp}(\Gamma_{j}(X))^{\circ} may be bigger: for instance if N=1N=1 Supp​(Γj​(X))∘\mathrm{Supp}(\Gamma_{j}(X))^{\circ} coincides with the big cone, and we can easily construct an example with p1,p2∈𝔹−​(L)p_{1},p_{2}\in\mathbbm{B}_{-}(L) and Δj​(L)∘≠∅\Delta_{j}(L)^{\circ}\neq\emptyset for j=1,2j=1,2. For instance take X=Blq​ℙ2X=\mathrm{Bl}_{q}\mathbbm{P}^{2}, L:=H+EL:=H+E where EE is the exceptional divisor and p1,p2∈Supp⁡(E)p_{1},p_{2}\in\mathrm{Supp}(E) different points. Then given two valuations associated to admissible flags Y⋅,jY_{\cdot,j} for j=1,2j=1,2 centered at p1,p2p_{1},p_{2} such that Y1,j=EY_{1,j}=E for any j=1,2j=1,2, it is easy to check that Δj​(L)∘≠∅\Delta_{j}(L)^{\circ}\neq\emptyset for j=1,2j=1,2 where by Lemma 3.6 this is equivalent to Δj​(L)≠∅\Delta_{j}(L)\neq\emptyset.

Proof.

For any vector a→∈ℕr\vec{a}\in\mathbbm{N}^{r} such that L:=a→⋅(L1,…,Lr)L:=\vec{a}\cdot(L_{1},\dots,L_{r}) is a big line bundle in Supp​(Γj​(X))∘\mathrm{Supp}(\Gamma_{j}(X))^{\circ}, we get Γj​(X)ℕ​a→=Γj​(L)\Gamma_{j}(X)_{\mathbbm{N}\vec{a}}=\Gamma_{j}(L), and so the base of the cone C⁡(Γj​(X)ℕ​a→)=C⁡(Γj​(L))⊂ℝn×ℝ​a→C(\Gamma_{j}(X)_{\mathbbm{N}\vec{a}})=C(\Gamma_{j}(L))\subset\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\mathbbm{R}\vec{a} is the multipoint Okounkov body Δj​(L)\Delta_{j}(L), i.e.

Δj​(L)=π⁡(C⁡(Γj​(X)ℕ​a→)∩(ℝn×{1})).\Delta_{j}(L)=\pi\Big(C(\Gamma_{j}(X)_{\mathbbm{N}\vec{a}})\cap\big(\mathbbm{R}^{n}\times\{1\}\big)\Big).

Then Proposition 3.14 implies that the right side of the last equality coincides with the fiber Δj​(X)\Delta_{j}(X) over c1​(L)c_{1}(L). Both sides rescale linearly, so the equality extends to ℚ\mathbbm{Q}-line bundles.
Next by Lemma 3.6 it follows that c1​(L)∈Supp⁡(Γj​(X))c_{1}(L)\in\mathrm{Supp}\big(\Gamma_{j}(X)\big) for any ℚ\mathbbm{Q}-line bundle LL such that Δj​(L)≠∅\Delta_{j}(L)\neq\emptyset. On the other hand, by the first part of the proof we get

Supp(Γj(X))∘∩N1(X)ℚ⊂{c1(L):Δj(L)≠∅,Lℚ−linebundle}.\mathrm{Supp}\big(\Gamma_{j}(X)\big)^{\circ}\cap\mathrm{N}^{1}(X)_{\mathbbm{Q}}\subset\{c_{1}(L)\,:\Delta_{j}(L)\neq\emptyset,L\,\,\mathbbm{Q}\mathrm{-line}\,\mathrm{bundle}\}. (6)

Thus it remains to prove that the right hand in (6)(\ref{eqn:Ref}) is open in N1​(X)ℚ\mathrm{N}^{1}(X)_{\mathbbm{Q}}, which is equivalent to show that Δj​(L−1k​A)≠∅\Delta_{j}(L-\frac{1}{k}A)\neq\emptyset for k≫1k\gg 1 big enough if AA is a fixed very ample line bundle since the ample cone is open and not empty in N1​(X)ℝ\mathrm{N}^{1}(X)_{\mathbbm{R}} and N1​(X)ℝ\mathrm{N}^{1}(X)_{\mathbbm{R}} is a finite dimensional vector space. Considering the multiplication by a section s∈H0​(X,A)s\in H^{0}(X,A) such that s⁡(pi)≠0s(p_{i})\neq 0 for any i=1,…,Ni=1,\dots,N, we obtain Δi​(L−1k​A)⊂Δi​(L)\Delta_{i}(L-\frac{1}{k}A)\subset\Delta_{i}(L) for any i=1,…,Ni=1,\dots,N. Therefore by Theorem A and Lemma 3.6 we necessarily have Δj​(L−1k​A)∘≠∅\Delta_{j}(L-\frac{1}{k}A)^{\circ}\neq\emptyset for k≫1k\gg 1 big enough since VolX​(L−1k​A)↗VolX​(L)\mathrm{Vol}_{X}(L-\frac{1}{k}A)\nearrow\mathrm{Vol}_{X}(L) and Δj​(L)∘≠∅\Delta_{j}(L)^{\circ}\neq\emptyset. This concludes the proof. ∎

As a consequence of Theorem 3.15, we can extend the definition of multipoint Okounkov bodies to ℝ\mathbbm{R}-line bundles. Indeed we can define Δj​(L)\Delta_{j}(L) as the limit (in the Hausdorff sense) of Δj​(Lk)\Delta_{j}(L_{k}) if c1(L)∈Supp(Γj(X))∘={c1(L):Δj(L)≠∅,Lℚ−linebundle}¯∘c_{1}(L)\in\mathrm{Supp}(\Gamma_{j}(X))^{\circ}=\overline{\{c_{1}(L)\,:\,\Delta_{j}(L)\neq\emptyset,L\,\mathbbm{Q}\mathrm{-line}\,\mathrm{bundle}\}}^{\circ} where {Lk}k∈ℕ\{L_{k}\}_{k\in\mathbbm{N}} is any sequence of ℚ\mathbbm{Q}-line bundles such that c1​(Lk)→c1​(L)c_{1}(L_{k})\to c_{1}(L), and Δj​(L)=∅\Delta_{j}(L)=\emptyset otherwise. This extension is well-defined and coherent with Lemma 3.6, since we obtain Δj​(L)∘≠∅\Delta_{j}(L)^{\circ}\neq\emptyset iff Δj​(L)≠∅\Delta_{j}(L)\neq\emptyset.

Corollary 3.17.

The function VolRn:Supp​(Γj​(X))∘→ℝ>0\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{R}^{n}}:\mathrm{Supp}(\Gamma_{j}(X))^{\circ}\to\mathbbm{R}_{>0}, c1​(L)→VolRn​(Δj​(L))c_{1}(L)\to\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{R}^{n}}(\Delta_{j}(L)) is well-defined, continuous, homogeneous of degree nn and log-concave, i.e.

VolRn​(Δj​(L+L′))1/n≥VolRn​(Δj​(L))1/n+VolRn​(Δj​(L′))1/n\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{R}^{n}}(\Delta_{j}(L+L^{\prime}))^{1/n}\geq\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{R}^{n}}(\Delta_{j}(L))^{1/n}+\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{R}^{n}}(\Delta_{j}(L^{\prime}))^{1/n}
Proof.

The fact that it is well-defined and its homogeneity follow directly from Propositions 3.10 and 3.11, while the other statements are standard in convex geometry, using the Brunn-Minkowski Theorem and Theorem 3.15. ∎

Finally we note that the Theorem 3.15 provides a description of the multipoint Okounkov bodies similarly to that of Theorem 2.9.(iii):

Corollary 3.18.

If L=𝒪X​(D)L=\mathcal{O}_{X}(D) is a big line bundle such that c1​(L)∈Supp​(Γj​(X))∘c_{1}(L)\in\mathrm{Supp}(\Gamma_{j}(X))^{\circ}, then

Δj(L)=νpj{D′∈Div≥0(X)ℝ:D′≡n​u​mDandνpj(D′)<νpi(D′)∀i≠j}¯.\Delta_{j}(L)=\overline{\nu^{p_{j}}\{D^{\prime}\in\mathrm{Div}_{\geq 0}(X)_{\mathbbm{R}}:D^{\prime}\equiv_{num}D\,\mathrm{and}\,\nu^{p_{j}}(D^{\prime})<\nu^{p_{i}}(D^{\prime})\,\forall i\neq j\}}.

In particular every rational point in Δj​(L)∘\Delta_{j}(L)^{\circ} is valuative and if it contains a small nn-symplex with valuative vertices then any rational point in the nn-symplex is valuative.

Proof.

The first part follows directly from Theorem 3.15 since D′≡n​u​mD{D^{\prime}\equiv_{num}D} iff c1​(L)=c1​(𝒪X​(D′))c_{1}(L)=c_{1}(\mathcal{O}_{X}(D^{\prime})) by definition (considering the ℝ−\mathbbm{R}-line bundle 𝒪X​(D′)\mathcal{O}_{X}(D^{\prime})). The second part about Δj​(L)∘\Delta_{j}(L)^{\circ} follows combining Lemma 3.6.(iii).(iii) and the multiplicative property of νpj\nu^{p_{j}} with Theorem 2.3 (see also the proof of Proposition 2.4). ∎

3.3 Geometry of multipoint Okounkov bodies

To investigate the geometry of the multipoint Okounkov bodies we need to introduce the following important invariant:

Definition 3.19.

Let LL be a line bundle, V⊂XV\subset X a subvariety of dimension dd and H0(X|V,kL):=Im(H0(X,kL)→H0(V,kL|V))H^{0}(X|V,kL):=\mathrm{Im}\Big(H^{0}(X,kL)\to H^{0}(V,kL_{|V})\Big). Then the quantity

VolX|V​(L):=lim supk→∞dimH0​(X|V,k​L)kd/d!\mathrm{Vol}_{X|V}(L):=\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{\dim H^{0}(X|V,kL)}{k^{d}/d!}

is called the restricted volume of LL along VV.

We refer to [ELMNP09] and reference therein for the theory about this new object.
In the repeatedly quoted paper [LM09], given a valuation νp​(s)=(νp​(s)1,…,νp​(s)n)\nu^{p}(s)=(\nu^{p}(s)_{1},\dots,\nu^{p}(s)_{n}) associated to an admissible flag Y⋅=(Y1,…,Yn)Y_{\cdot}=(Y_{1},\dots,Y_{n}) such that Y1=DY_{1}=D and a line bundle LL such that D⊄𝔹+​(L)D\not\subset\mathbbm{B}_{+}(L), the authors also defined the one-point Okounkov body of the graded linear sistem H0(X|D,kL)⊂H0(D,kL|D)H^{0}(X|D,kL)\subset H^{0}(D,kL_{|D}) by

ΔX|D​(L):=Δ⁡(ΓX|D)\Delta_{X|D}(L):=\Delta(\Gamma_{X|D})

with ΓX|D:={(νp(s)2,…,νp(s)n,k)∈ℕn−1×ℕ:s∈H0(X|D,kL)∖{0},k≥1}\Gamma_{X|D}:=\{(\nu^{p}(s)_{2},\dots,\nu^{p}(s)_{n},k)\in\mathbbm{N}^{n-1}\times\mathbbm{N}:{s\in H^{0}(X|D,kL)\setminus\{0\}},{k\geq 1\}} and they proved the following result.

Theorem 3.20 ([LM09], Theorem 4.244.24, Corollary 4.254.25).

4.1 Ample case

For any finite set 𝒜⊂ℕm\mathcal{A}\subset\mathbbm{N}^{m} with a fixed additive total order >>, there exists γ∈(ℕ>0)m\gamma\in(\mathbbm{N}_{>0})^{m} such that

4.2 The big case

Definition 4.6.

If LL is big, we say that a finite family of n−n-dimensional Kähler manifolds {(Mj,ηj)}j=1N\{(M_{j},\eta_{j})\}_{j=1}^{N} packs into (X,L)(X,L) if for every family of relatively compact open set Uj⋐MjU_{j}\Subset M_{j} there is a holomorphic embedding f:⨆j=1NUj→Xf:\bigsqcup_{j=1}^{N}U_{j}\to X and there exists a kähler current with analytical singularities TT lying in c1​(L)c_{1}(L) such that f∗ηj=T|f(Uj)f_{*}\eta_{j}=T_{|f(U_{j})}. If, in addition,

∑j=1N∫Mjηjn=∫Xc1​(L)n\sum_{j=1}^{N}\int_{M_{j}}\eta_{j}^{n}=\int_{X}c_{1}(L)^{n}

then we say that {(Mj,ηj)}j=1N\{(M_{j},\eta_{j})\}_{j=1}^{N} packs perfectly into (X,L)(X,L).

Reasoning as in the previous section we prove the following result.

Theorem 3 (Big Case).

Let LL be a big line bundle. Then {(Ωj​(L),ωs​t)}j=1N\{(\Omega_{j}(L),\omega_{st})\}_{j=1}^{N} packs perfectly into (X,L)(X,L).

Proof.

By Lemma 3.6, Ωj​(L)=∅\Omega_{j}(L)=\emptyset for any jj such that Δj​(L)∘=∅\Delta_{j}(L)^{\circ}=\emptyset. So, unless removing some of the points we may assume that Δj​(L)∘≠∅\Delta_{j}(L)^{\circ}\neq\emptyset for any j=1,…,Nj=1,\dots,N.
Thus letting k≫0k\gg 0 big enough such that Δjk​(L)e​s​s≠∅\Delta_{j}^{k}(L)^{ess}\neq\emptyset for any jj (Proposition 2.5) we can proceed similarly to the proof of Theorem 4.4 with the unique difference that ln⁡(∑i=1N∑α𝐢∈𝒜i|sα𝐢τγ⋅α𝐢|2)\ln\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sum_{\mathbf{\alpha_{i}}\in\mathcal{A}_{i}}\lvert\frac{s_{\mathbf{\alpha_{i}}}}{\tau^{\gamma\cdot\mathbf{\alpha_{i}}}}\rvert^{2}\Big) extends to a positive singular hermitian metric, hence we get a (current of) curvature TT that is a Kähler current with analytical singularities. Next, as in the ample case, we can show that {(Ωj​(L),ωs​t)}j=1N\{(\Omega_{j}(L),\omega_{st})\}_{j=1}^{N} packs perfectly into (X,L)(X,L).∎

Remark 4.7.

If the family of valuations fixed is associated to a family of admissible flags Yj,i={zj,1=⋯=zj,i=0}Y_{j,i}=\{z_{j,1}=\dots=z_{j,i}=0\} then each associated embedding f:⨆j=1NUj→Xf:\bigsqcup_{j=1}^{N}U_{j}\to X can be chosen so that

f|f(Uj)−1(Yj,i)={zj,1=⋯=zj,i=0}f^{-1}_{|f(U_{j})}(Y_{j,i})=\{z_{j,1}=\cdots=z_{j,i}=0\}

In particular if N=1N=1 we recover the Theorem CC in [WN15].

5 Local Positivity

5.1 Moving Multipoint Seshadri Constant

Definition 5.1.

Let LL be a nef line bundle on XX. The quantity

ϵS​(L,p1,…,pN):=infL⋅C∑i=1Nmultpi​C\epsilon_{S}(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}):=\inf\frac{L\cdot C}{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathrm{mult}_{p_{i}}C}

where the infimum is over all irreducible curves C⊂XC\subset X passing through at least one of the points p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} is called the multipoint Seshadri constant at p1,…,pN\mathbf{p_{1},\dots,p_{N}} of 𝐋\mathbf{L}.

This constant has played an important role in the last three decades and it is the natural extension of the Seshadri constant introduced by Demailly in [Dem90].
The following Lemma is well-known and its proof can be found for instance in [Laz04], [BDRH+09]:

Lemma 5.2.

Let LL be a nef line bundle on XX. Then

ϵS​(L,p1,…,pN)=sup{t≥0:μ∗​L−t​∑i=1NEi​is​nef}=inf(LdimV⋅V∑j=1Nmultpj​V)1dimV\epsilon_{S}(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})=\sup\Big\{t\geq 0\,:\,\mu^{*}L-t\sum_{i=1}^{N}E_{i}\,\,\mathrm{is}\,\,\mathrm{nef}\Big\}=\inf\Big(\frac{L^{\dim V}\cdot V}{\sum_{j=1}^{N}\mathrm{mult}_{p_{j}}V}\Big)^{\frac{1}{\dim V}}

where μ:X~→X\mu:\tilde{X}\to X is the blow-up at Z={p1,…,pN}Z=\{p_{1},\dots,p_{N}\}, EiE_{i} is the exceptional divisor above pip_{i} and where the infimum on the right side is over all positive dimensional irreducible subvarieties VV containing at least one point among p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N}.

The characterization of Lemma 5.2 allows to extend the definition to nef ℚ−\mathbbm{Q}-line bundles by homogeneity and to nef ℝ−\mathbbm{R}-line bundles by continuity.

Here we describe a possible generalization of the multipoint Seshadri constant for big line bundles:

Definition 5.3.

Let LL be a big ℝ−\mathbbm{R}-line bundle, we define the moving multipoint Seshadri constant at p1,…,pN\mathbf{p_{1},\dots,p_{N}} of 𝐋\mathbf{L} as

ϵS​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN):=supf∗​L=A+EϵS​(A,f−1​(p1),…,f−1​(pN))\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}):=\sup_{f^{*}L=A+E}\epsilon_{S}(A;f^{-1}(p_{1}),\dots,f^{-1}(p_{N}))

if p1,…,pN∉𝔹+​(L)p_{1},\dots,p_{N}\notin\mathbbm{B}_{+}(L) and as ϵS​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN):=0\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}):=0 otherwise, where the supremum is taken over all projective morphisms f:Y→Xf:Y\to X with YY smooth such that ff is an isomorphism around p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} and over all decomposition f∗​L=A+Ef^{*}L=A+E where AA is an ample ℚ−\mathbbm{Q}-divisor and EE is effective with f−1​(pj)∉Supp⁡(E)f^{-1}(p_{j})\notin\mathrm{Supp}(E) for any j=1,…,Nj=1,\dots,N.

For N=1N=1, we retrieve the definition given in [ELMNP09].

The following properties are well-known for the one-point case.

Proposition 5.4.

Let L,L′L,L^{\prime} be big ℝ−\mathbbm{R}-line bundles. Then

  • i)

    ϵS​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN)≤(VolX​(L)N)1/n\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})\leq\big(\frac{\mathrm{Vol}_{X}(L)}{N}\big)^{1/n};

  • ii)

    if c1​(L)=c1​(L′)c_{1}(L)=c_{1}(L^{\prime}) then ϵS​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN)=ϵS​(‖L′‖,p1,…,pN)\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})=\epsilon_{S}(||L^{\prime}||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N});

  • iii)

    ϵS​(‖λ​L‖,p1,…,pN)=λ​ϵS​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN)\epsilon_{S}(||\lambda L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})=\lambda\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}) for any λ∈ℝ>0\lambda\in\mathbbm{R}_{>0};

  • iv)

    if p1,…,pN∉𝔹+​(L)∪𝔹+​(L′)p_{1},\dots,p_{N}\notin\mathbbm{B}_{+}(L)\cup\mathbbm{B}_{+}(L^{\prime}) then ϵS​(‖L+L′‖,p1,…,pN)≥ϵS​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN)+ϵS​(‖L′‖,p1,…,pN)\epsilon_{S}(||L+L^{\prime}||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})\geq\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})+\epsilon_{S}(||L^{\prime}||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}).

Proof.

Combining the definition of the moving multipoint Seshadri constant with Lemma 5.2, the first three points are immediate since ampleness and nefness are numerical conditions and the ample, nef classes form the so-called ample and nef cones. More precisely, for a projective morphism f:Y→Xf:Y\to X and an ample ℚ\mathbbm{Q}-divisor as in the definition, the homogeneity of ϵS​(A,f−1​(p1),…,f−1​(pN))\epsilon_{S}\big(A;f^{-1}(p_{1}),\dots,f^{-1}(p_{N})\big) is given by the first equality of Lemma 5.2 while the second equality of the same Lemma 5.2 yields ϵS​(A,f−1​(p1),…,f−1​(pN))≤(An/N)1/n≤(VolX​(L)/N)1/n\epsilon_{S}\big(A;f^{-1}(p_{1}),\dots,f^{-1}(p_{N})\big)\leq\big(A^{n}/N\big)^{1/n}\leq\big(\mathrm{Vol}_{X}(L)/N\big)^{1/n}.
Regarding the last point, fix A,A′A,A^{\prime} ample ℚ\mathbbm{Q}-divisors as in the definition of the moving multipoint Seshadri constant for L,L′L,L^{\prime} with respect to projective morphisms f:Y→X,f′:Y′→Xf:Y\to X,f^{\prime}:Y^{\prime}\to X. Then taking projective morphisms g:W→Y,g′:W→Y′g:W\to Y,g^{\prime}:W\to Y^{\prime} which are isomorphism around p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N}, there exist effective divisors F,F′F,F^{\prime} on WW such that g−1​f−1​(pj)∉Supp⁡(F)g^{-1}f^{-1}(p_{j})\notin\mathrm{Supp}(F) (and similarly for F′F^{\prime}) and decreasing sequences converging to 00 of positive rational numbers {am}m∈ℕ,{am′}m∈ℕ⊂ℚ>0\{a_{m}\}_{m\in\mathbbm{N}},\{a_{m}^{\prime}\}_{m\in\mathbbm{N}}\subset\mathbbm{Q}_{>0} such that Bm:=g∗​A−am​FB_{m}:=g^{*}A-a_{m}F, Bm′:=g′⁣∗​A′−am′​F′B_{m}^{\prime}:=g^{\prime*}A^{\prime}-a_{m}^{\prime}F^{\prime} are ample ℚ\mathbbm{Q}-divisors for any m∈ℕm\in\mathbbm{N}. Then we claim that

as m→∞m\to\infty, and similarly for A′,Bm′A^{\prime},B^{\prime}_{m}. Thus, for any δ>0\delta>0 fixed, we can choose A,A′,f,f′,m,m′A,A^{\prime},f,f^{\prime},m,m^{\prime} such that

We check that the moving multipoint Seshadri constant is an effective generalization of the multipoint Seshadri constant:
