Theorem 5.8.

Let p1,…,pN∈Xp_{1},\dots,p_{N}\in X be different points. Then the function N1​(X)ℝ∋L→ϵS​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN)∈ℝ{\mathrm{N}^{1}(X)_{\mathbbm{R}}\ni L\to\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})\in\mathbbm{R}} is continuous.

Proof.

The homogeneity and the concavity described in Proposition 5.4 implies the locally uniform continuity of ϵS​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN)\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}) on the open convex subset (⋃j=1NB+​(pj))C\big(\bigcup_{j=1}^{N}B_{+}(p_{j})\big)^{C} (see Remark 3.16). Thus it is sufficient to show that limL′→LϵS​(‖L′‖,p1,…,pN)=0\lim_{L^{\prime}\to L}\epsilon_{S}(||L^{\prime}||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})=0 if c1​(L)∈⋃j=1NB+​(pj)c_{1}(L)\in\bigcup_{j=1}^{N}B_{+}(p_{j}). But, letting V⊂XV\subset X be an irreducible component of 𝔹+​(L)\mathbbm{B}_{+}(L) containing at least one of the points p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N}, we have

limL′→LϵS​(‖L′‖,p1,…,pN)≤limL′→L(VolX|V​(L′)∑j=1Nmultpj​V)1/dimV=0\lim_{L^{\prime}\to L}\epsilon_{S}(\|L^{\prime}\|;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})\leq\lim_{L^{\prime}\to L}\Bigg(\frac{\mathrm{Vol}_{X|V}(L^{\prime})}{\sum_{j=1}^{N}\mathrm{mult}_{p_{j}}V}\Bigg)^{1/\dim V}=0

where the inequality follows from Proposition 5.7 while the convergence is a consequence of the continuity of the restricted volume (see [ELMNP09], in particular Theorem 5.7.5.7. in [ELMNP09]). ∎

To conclude the section we recall that for a line bundle LL and for an integer s∈ℤ≥0s\in\mathbbm{Z}_{\geq 0}, we say that LL generates the s−s-jets at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} if the map

H0​(X,L)↠⨁j=1NH0​(X,L⊗𝒪X,pj/𝔪pjs+1)H^{0}(X,L)\twoheadrightarrow\bigoplus_{j=1}^{N}H^{0}(X,L\otimes\mathcal{O}_{X,p_{j}}/\mathfrak{m}_{p_{j}}^{s+1})

is surjective where we have set 𝔪pj\mathfrak{m}_{p_{j}} for the maximal ideal in 𝒪X,pj\mathcal{O}_{X,p_{j}}. We report an useful last characterization of the moving multipoint Seshadri constant.

Proposition 5.9 ([Ito13], Lemma 3.10.3.10.).

Let LL be a big line bundle. Then

ϵS​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN)=supk>0s⁡(k​L,p1,…,pN)k=limk→∞s⁡(k​L,p1,…,pN)k\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})=\sup_{k>0}\frac{s(kL;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})}{k}=\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{s(kL;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})}{k}

where s⁡(k​L,p1,…,pN)s(kL;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}) is 00 if k​LkL does not generate then s−s-jets at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} for any s∈ℤ≥0s\in\mathbbm{Z}_{\geq 0}, otherwise it is the biggest non-negative integer such that k​LkL generates the s⁡(k​L,p1,…,pN)−s(kL;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})-jets at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N}.

5.2 Proof of Theorem B

We prove here one of our main results.

Theorem B.

Let LL be a big line bundle and let >> be the deglex order. Then

ϵϵ​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN)=max⁡{0,ξ⁡(L,p1,…,pN)}\epsilon_{\epsilon}(\|L\|;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})=\max\big\{0,\xi(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})\big\}

where ξ(L;p1,…,pN):=sup{t≥0:tΣn⊂Δj(L)e​s​sfor anyj=1,…,N}\xi(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}):=\sup\{t\geq 0\,:\,t\Sigma_{n}\subset\Delta_{j}(L)^{ess}\,\mbox{for any}\,j=1,\dots,N\} and Σn\Sigma_{n} is the unit nn-symplex.

Namely we construct the multipoint Okounkov bodies Δj​(L)\Delta_{j}(L) from a family of valuations νpj\nu^{p_{j}} associated to a family of infinitesimal flags centered at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} (see paragraphs §\lx@sectionsign 2.4 and §\lx@sectionsign 3.5).
Observe that for N=1N=1, Theorem B recovers Theorem C in [KL17].

Before proceeding with the proof, in the spirit of the aforementioned work of Demailly [Dem90], we need to describe the moving multipoint Seshadri constant ϵ⁡(‖L‖,p1,…,pN)\epsilon(||L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}) in a more analytical language.

Definition 5.10.

We say that a singular metric φ\varphi of a line bundle LL has isolated logarithmic poles at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} of coefficient γ\gamma if min⁡{ν⁡(φ,p1),…,ν⁡(φ,pN)}=γ\min\{\nu(\varphi,p_{1}),\dots,\nu(\varphi,p_{N})\}=\gamma and φ\varphi is finite and continuous in a small punctured neighborhood Vj∖{pj}V_{j}\setminus\{p_{j}\} for every j=1,…,Nj=1,\dots,N. We have denoted by ν⁡(φ,pj)\nu(\varphi,p_{j}) the Lelong number of φ\varphi at pjp_{j},

ν⁡(φ,pj):=lim infz→xφj​(z)ln⁡|z−x|2\nu(\varphi,p_{j}):=\liminf_{z\to x}\frac{\varphi_{j}(z)}{\ln\lvert z-x\rvert^{2}}

where φj\varphi_{j} is the local plurisubharmonic function defining φ\varphi around pj=x{p_{j}=x}.
We set γ(L;p1,…,pN):=sup{γ∈ℝ:L\gamma(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}):=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbbm{R}\,:\,L has a positive singular metric with isolated logarithmic poles at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} of coefficient γ}\gamma\}

Note that for N=1N=1 we recover the definition given in [Dem90].

Proposition 5.11.

Let LL be a big ℚ−\mathbbm{Q}-line bundle. Then

γ⁡(L,p1,…,pN)=ϵS​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN)\gamma(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})=\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})
Proof.

By homogeneity we can assume LL to be a line bundle, and we fix a family of local holomorphic coordinates {zj,1,…,zj,n}\{z_{j,1},\dots,z_{j,n}\} in open coordinated sets U1,…,UNU_{1},\dots,U_{N} centered respectively at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N}.
Setting zj:=(zj,1,…,zj,N)z_{j}:=(z_{j,1},\dots,z_{j,N}) and s:=s⁡(k​L,p1,…,pN)s:=s(kL;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}) for k≥1k\geq 1 natural number, we can find holomorphic section fαf_{\alpha}, parametrized by all α=(α1,…,αN)∈ℕN​n\alpha=(\alpha_{1},\dots,\alpha_{N})\in\mathbbm{N}^{Nn} such that |αj|=s\lvert\alpha_{j}\rvert=s and fα|Uj=zjαjf_{\alpha|U_{j}}=z_{j}^{\alpha_{j}} for any j=1,…,Nj=1,\dots,N. In other words, we can find holomorphic sections of k​LkL whose jets at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} generates all possible combination of monomials of degree ss around the points chosen. Thus the positive singular metric φ\varphi on LL given by

φ:=1k​log⁡(∑α|fα|2)\varphi:=\frac{1}{k}\log\Big(\sum_{\alpha}\lvert f_{\alpha}\rvert^{2}\Big)

has isolated logarithmic poles at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} of coefficient s/ks/k. Hence γ⁡(L,p1,…,pN)≥s⁡(k​L,p1,…,pN)/k\gamma(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})\geq s(kL;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})/k, and letting k→∞k\to\infty Proposition 5.9 yields γ⁡(L,p1,…,pN)≥ϵS​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN)\gamma(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})\geq\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}).
Conversely, assuming γ⁡(L,p1,…,pN)>0\gamma(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})>0, let {γt}t∈ℕ⊂ℚ\{\gamma_{t}\}_{t\in\mathbbm{N}}\subset\mathbbm{Q} be an increasing sequence of rational numbers converging to γ⁡(L,p1,…,pN)\gamma(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}) and let {kt}t∈ℕ\{k_{t}\}_{t\in\mathbbm{N}} be an increasing sequence of natural numbers such that {kt​γt}t∈ℕ\{k_{t}\gamma_{t}\}_{t\in\mathbbm{N}} converges to +∞+\infty. Moreover let AA be an ample line bundle such that A−KXA-K_{X} is ample, and let ω=d​dc​ϕ\omega=dd^{c}\phi be a Kähler form in the class c1​(A−KX)c_{1}(A-K_{X}).
Thus for any positive singular metric φt\varphi_{t} of LL with isolated logarithmic poles at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} of coefficient ≥γt\geq\gamma_{t}, kt​φt+ϕk_{t}\varphi_{t}+\phi is a positive singular metric of kt​L+A−KXk_{t}L+A-K_{X} with Kähler current d​dc​(kt​φt)+ωdd^{c}(k_{t}\varphi_{t})+\omega as curvature and with isolated logarithmic poles at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} of coefficient ≥kt​γt\geq k_{t}\gamma_{t}. Therefore, for t≫1t\gg 1 big enough, kt​Lt+Ak_{t}L_{t}+A generates all (kt​γt−n)−(k_{t}\gamma_{t}-n)-jets at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} by Corollary 3.3. in [Dem90], and thanks to Proposition 5.9 we obtain

ϵS​(‖L+1kt​A‖,p1,…,pN)≥kt​γt−nkt=γt−nkt.\epsilon_{S}\Big(\big\|L+\frac{1}{k_{t}}A\big\|;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}\Big)\geq\frac{k_{t}\gamma_{t}-n}{k_{t}}=\gamma_{t}-\frac{n}{k_{t}}.

Letting t→∞t\to\infty we get ϵS​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN)≥γ⁡(L,p1,…,pN)\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})\geq\gamma(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}) exploiting the continuity of Theorem 5.8. ∎

Remark 5.12.

Observe that the same result cannot hold if we restrict ourselves to considering metrics with logarithmic poles at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} not necessarily isolated. Indeed Demailly in [Dem93] showed that for any nef and big ℚ−\mathbbm{Q}-line bundle LL over a projective manifold, for any different points p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N}, and for any τ1,…,τN\tau_{1},\dots,\tau_{N} positive real numbers with ∑j=1Nτjn<(Ln)\sum_{j=1}^{N}\tau_{j}^{n}<(L^{n}) there exists a positive singular metric φ\varphi with logarithmic poles at any pjp_{j} of coefficients, respectively, τj\tau_{j}. We thus conclude that the result in Proposition 5.11 holds considering metrics with logarithmic poles at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} not necessarily isolated if and only if the multipoint Seshadri constant is maximal, i.e. ϵS​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN)=(VolX​(L)/N)1/n\epsilon_{S}(||L||,p_{1},\dots,p_{N})=(\mathrm{Vol}_{X}(L)/N)^{1/n}.

Proof of Theorem B.

By the continuity of Theorems 3.15, 5.8 and by the homogeneity of both sides we can assume LL big line bundle. Moreover we may also assume Δj​(L)∘≠∅\Delta_{j}(L)^{\circ}\neq\emptyset for any j=1,…,Nj=1,\dots,N since otherwise the statement is a consequence of Lemma 3.6.(ii).

Remark 5.13.

In the case LL ample line bundle, to prove the inequality ϵS​(L,p1,…,pN)≥ξ⁡(L,p1,…,pN){\epsilon_{S}(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})\geq\xi(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})} we could have used Theorem 3. The proof of the Theorem B shows that ξ⁡(L,p1,…,pN)\xi(L;p_{1},\dots,p_{N}) is independent from the choice of the family of valuations given by the associated infinitesimal flags.

The following corollary, which is an immediate consequence of Theorems B, 3 extends Theorem 0.50.5 in [Eckl17] to all dimensions (as Eckl claimed in his paper) and to big line bundles.

Corollary 5.15.

Let LL be a big line bundle. Then

ϵS​(‖L‖,p1,…,pN)=max{0,sup{r>0:Br(0)⊂Ωj(L)∀j=1,…,N}}==max{0,sup{r>0:{(Br(0),ωs​t​d)}j=1Npacks into(X,L)}.\sqrt{\epsilon_{S}(||L||;p_{1},\dots,p_{N})}=\max\Big\{0,\sup\{r>0\,:\,B_{r}(0)\subset\Omega_{j}(L)\,\,\forall\,j=1,\dots,N\}\Big\}=\\ =\max\Big\{0,\sup\big\{r>0\,:\,\{(B_{r}(0),\omega_{std}\big)\}_{j=1}^{N}\,\mbox{packs into}\,(X,L)\,\big\}.

For N=1N=1 it is the content of Theorem 1.3.1.3. in [WN15].

6 Some particular cases

6.1 Projective toric manifolds

In this section X=XΔX=X_{\Delta} is a smooth projective toric variety associated to a fan Δ\Delta in Nℝ≃ℝnN_{\mathbbm{R}}\simeq\mathbbm{R}^{n}, so that the torus TN:=N⊗ℤℂ∗≃(ℂ∗)nT_{N}:=N\otimes_{\mathbbm{Z}}\mathbbm{C}^{*}\simeq(\mathbbm{C}^{*})^{n} acts on XX (N≃ℤnN\simeq\mathbbm{Z}^{n} denote a lattice of rank nn with dual M:=Homℤ​(N,ℤ)M:=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbbm{Z}}(N,\mathbbm{Z}), see [Ful93], [Cox11] for notation and basic fact about toric varieties).
It is well-known that there is a correspondence between toric manifolds XX polarized by TN−T_{N}-invariant ample divisors DD and lattice polytopes P⊂MℝP\subset M_{\mathbbm{R}} of dimension nn. Indeed to any such divisor D=∑ρ∈Δ⁡(1)aρ​Dρ{D=\sum_{\rho\in\Delta(1)}a_{\rho}D_{\rho}}, denoting by Δ⁡(k)\Delta(k) the cones of dimension kk, the polytope PDP_{D} is given by PD:=⋂ρ∈Δ⁡(1){m∈Mℝ:⟨m,vρ⟩≥−aρ}P_{D}:=\bigcap_{\rho\in\Delta(1)}\{m\in M_{\mathbbm{R}}\,:\,\langle m,v_{\rho}\rangle\geq-a_{\rho}\} where vρv_{\rho} represents the generator of ρ∩N\rho\cap N. Conversely any such polytope PP can be described as P:=⋂F​facet{m∈Mℝ:⟨m,nF⟩≥−aF}P:=\bigcap_{F\,\mathrm{facet}}\{m\in M_{\mathbbm{R}}\,:\,\langle m,n_{F}\rangle\geq-a_{F}\} where a facet is a 1−1-codimensional face of PP and nF∈Nn_{F}\in N is the unique primitive element that is normal to FF and that points toward the interior of PP. Thus the normal fan associated to PP is ΔP:={σℱ:ℱ​face​of​P}\Delta_{P}:=\{\sigma_{\mathcal{F}}\,:\,\mathcal{F}\,\mathrm{face}\,\mathrm{of}\,P\} where σℱ\sigma_{\mathcal{F}} is the cone in ℕℝ\mathbbm{N}_{\mathbbm{R}} generated by all normal elements nFn_{F} as above for any facet containing the face ℱ\mathcal{F}. In particular vertices of PP correspond to TN−T_{N}-invariant points on the toric manifold XPX_{P} associated to ΔP\Delta_{P} while facets of PP correspond to TN−T_{N}-invariant divisors on XPX_{P}. Finally the polarization is given by DP:=∑F​facetaF​DFD_{P}:=\sum_{F\,\mathrm{facet}}a_{F}D_{F}.

Thus, given an ample toric line bundle L=𝒪X​(D)L=\mathcal{O}_{X}(D) on a projective toric manifold XX we can fix local holomorphic coordinates around a TN−T_{N}-invariant point p∈Xp\in X (corresponding to a vertex xσ∈Px_{\sigma}\in P) such that {zi=0}=Di|Uσ\{z_{i}=0\}=D_{i|U_{\sigma}} for DiD_{i} TN−T_{N}-invariant divisors and we can assume D|Uσ=0D_{|U_{\sigma}}=0.

In the setting as above, the equality

ϕℝn​(PD)=Δ⁡(L)\phi_{\mathbbm{R}^{n}}(P_{D})=\Delta(L)

holds, where ϕℝ\phi_{\mathbbm{R}} is the linear map associated to ϕ:M→ℤn,ϕ⁡(m):=(⟨m,v1⟩,…,⟨m,vn⟩)\phi:M\to\mathbbm{Z}^{n},\phi(m):=(\langle m,v_{1}\rangle,\dots,\langle m,v_{n}\rangle), for vi∈ΔPD​(1)v_{i}\in\Delta_{P_{D}}(1) generators of the ray associated to DiD_{i}, and Δ⁡(L)\Delta(L) is the one-point Okounkov body associated to the admissible flag given by the local holomorphic coordinates chosen.

(Lemma 4.2.1, [BDRH+09]) Let (X,L)(X,L) be a toric polarized manifold, and let PP be the associated polytope with vertices xσ1,…,xσlx_{\sigma_{1}},\dots,x_{\sigma_{l}}. Remark 6.3.

By assumption, we know that PP is a Delzant polypote, i.e. there are exactly nn edges originating from each vertex, and the first integer points on such edges form a lattice basis (for integer we mean a point belonging in M). Moreover if one fixes the first integer points on the edges starting from a vertex xσx_{\sigma} (i.e. a basis for M​≃ℤnM\mathop{\simeq}\mathbbm{Z}^{n}), then the length of an edge starting from xσx_{\sigma} is defined as the usual length in ℝn\mathbbm{R}^{n}. Observe that the length of any edge is an integer since the polytope is a lattice polytope.

Similarly to Proposition 6.1, chosen RR TN−T_{N}-invariants points corresponding to RR vertices of the polytope PP, we retrieve the multipoint Okounkov bodies of the corresponding RR TN−T_{N}-invariant points on XX directly from the polytope:

Theorem 6.4.

Let (X,L)(X,L) be a toric polarized manifold, and let PP be the associated polytope with vertices xσ1,…,xσlx_{\sigma_{1}},\dots,x_{\sigma_{l}} corresponding, respectively, to the TN−T_{N}-points p1,…,plp_{1},\dots,p_{l}. we get by Proposition 2.4 ϕℝn,j​(Pj)=Δj​(L)\phi_{\mathbbm{R}^{n},j}(P_{j})=\Delta_{j}(L) since any valuative point in Hδ1,1∩⋯∩HδR,R∩PH_{\delta_{1},1}\cap\cdots\cap H_{\delta_{R},R}\cap P belongs to Δj​(L)\Delta_{j}(L) if δj<δi\delta_{j}<\delta_{i} for any i≠ji\neq j, while on the other hand any valuative point in Δj​(L)\Delta_{j}(L) belongs to Hδ1,1∩⋯∩HδR,R∩PH_{\delta_{1},1}\cap\cdots\cap H_{\delta_{R},R}\cap P for certain rational numbers δ1,…,δR\delta_{1},\dots,\delta_{R} such that δj≤δi\delta_{j}\leq\delta_{i}. ∎

As an easy consequence, we get that for any polarized toric manifold (X,L)(X,L) and for any choice of RR TN−T_{N}-invariants points p1,…,pRp_{1},\dots,p_{R}, the multipoint Okounkov bodies constructed from the infinitesimal flags as in Theorem 6.4 are polyhedral.

6.2 Surfaces

When XX has dimension 22, the following famous decomposition holds.

Theorem 6.8 (Zariski decomposition).

Let LL be a pseudoeffective ℚ−\mathbbm{Q}-line bundle on a surface XX. Then there exist ℚ−\mathbbm{Q}-line bundles P,NP,N such that

  • i)

    L=P+NL=P+N;

  • ii)

    PP is nef;

  • iii)

    NN is effective;

  • iv)

    H0​(X,k​P)≃H0​(X,k​L)H^{0}(X,kP)\simeq H^{0}(X,kL) for any k≥1k\geq 1;

  • v)

    P⋅E=0P\cdot E=0 for any EE irreducible curve contained in Supp⁡(N)\mathrm{Supp}(N).

Moreover we recall that by the main theorem of [BKS04] there exists a locally finite decomposition of the big cone into rational polyhedral subcones (Zariski chambers) such that in each interior of these subcones the negative part of the Zariski decomposition has constant support and the restricted and augmented base loci are equal (i.e. the divisors with cohomology classes in a interior of some Zariski chambers are stable, see [ELMNP06]).
Similarly to Theorem 6.4. in [LM09] and the first part of Theorem B in [KLM12] we describe the multipoint Okounkov bodies as follows:

Theorem 6.9.

Let LL be a big line bundle over a surface XX, let p1,…,pN∈Xp_{1},\dots,p_{N}\in X, and let νpj\nu^{p_{j}} be a family of valuations associated to admissible flags centered at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} with Y1,j=Ci|UpjY_{1,j}=C_{i|U_{p_{j}}} for irreducible curves CjC_{j}, j=1,…,Nj=1,\dots,N. Then for any j=1,…,Nj=1,\dots,N such that Δj​(L)∘≠∅\Delta_{j}(L)^{\circ}\neq\emptyset there exist piecewise linear functions αj,βj:[tj,−,tj,+]→ℝ≥0{\alpha_{j},\beta_{j}:[t_{j,-},t_{j,+}]\to\mathbbm{R}_{\geq 0}} for

0≤tj,−:=inf{t≥0:Cj⊄𝔹+​(L−t​𝔾)}<tj,+:=sup{t≥0:Cj⊄𝔹+​(L−t​𝔾)}≤≤μ⁡(L,𝔾):=sup{t≥0:L−t​𝔾​is​big}0\leq t_{j,-}:=\inf\{t\geq 0\,:\,C_{j}\not\subset\mathbbm{B}_{+}(L-t\mathbbm{G})\}<t_{j,+}:=\sup\{t\geq 0\,:\,C_{j}\not\subset\mathbbm{B}_{+}(L-t\mathbbm{G})\}\leq\\ \leq\mu(L;\mathbbm{G}):=\sup\{t\geq 0\,:\,L-t\mathbbm{G}\,\mathrm{is}\,\mathrm{big}\}

Thus by Theorem 3.21 and Lemma 6.3. in [LM09] we easily obtain Δj​(L)={(t,y)∈ℝ2:tj,−≤t≤tj,+​and​αj​(t)≤y≤βj​(t)}\Delta_{j}(L)=\{(t,y)\in\mathbbm{R}^{2}\,:\,t_{j,-}\leq t\leq t_{j,+}\,\mathrm{and}\,\alpha_{j}(t)\leq y\leq\beta_{j}(t)\} defining αj​(t):=ordpj​(Nt|Cj)\alpha_{j}(t):=\mathrm{ord}_{p_{j}}(N_{t|C_{j}}) and βj​(t):=ordpj​(Nt|Cj)+(Pt⋅Cj)\beta_{j}(t):=\mathrm{ord}_{p_{j}}(N_{t|C_{j}})+(P_{t}\cdot C_{j}) for Pt+NtP_{t}+N_{t} Zariski decomposition of L−t​𝔾L-t\mathbbm{G} (NtN_{t} can be restricted to CjC_{j} since Supp⁡(Nt)=𝔹−​(L−t​𝔾)\mathrm{Supp}(N_{t})=\mathbbm{B}_{-}(L-t\mathbbm{G})).

Thus the function s→Ns′{s\to N^{\prime}_{s}} is decreasing, i.e. Ns′′−Ns′N^{\prime}_{s^{\prime}}-N^{\prime}_{s} is effective for any 0≤s′<s≤tj,+−tj,−{0\leq s^{\prime}<s\leq t_{j,+}-t_{j,-}}, where Ls′=Ps′+Ns′L^{\prime}_{s}=P^{\prime}_{s}+N^{\prime}_{s} is the Zariski decomposition of Ls′L^{\prime}_{s}. Remark 6.10.

We observe that Δj​(L)∩[0,μ⁡(L,𝔾)−ϵ]×ℝ\Delta_{j}(L)\cap[0,\mu(L;\mathbbm{G})-\epsilon]\times\mathbbm{R} is rational polyhedral for any 0<ϵ<μ⁡(L,𝔾)0<\epsilon<\mu(L;\mathbbm{G}) thanks to the proof and to the main theorem in [BKS04].

A particular case is when p1,…,pN∉𝔹+​(L)p_{1},\dots,p_{N}\notin\mathbbm{B}_{+}(L) and νpj\nu^{p_{j}} is a family of valuations associated to infinitesimal flags centered respectively at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N}. Indeed in this case on the blow-up X~=Bl{p1,…,pN}​X\tilde{X}=\mathrm{Bl}_{\{p_{1},\dots,p_{N}\}}X we can consider the family of valuations ν~p~j\tilde{\nu}^{\tilde{p}_{j}} associated to the admissible flags centered respectively at points p~1,…,p~N∈X~\tilde{p}_{1},\dots,\tilde{p}_{N}\in\tilde{X} (see paragraph §\lx@sectionsign2.4). Observe that Y~1,j=Ej\tilde{Y}_{1,j}=E_{j} are the exceptional divisors over the points.

About the Nagata’s Conjecture:

One modern version of the Nagata’s conjecture says that for a choice of very general points p1,…,pN∈ℙ2{p_{1},\dots,p_{N}\in\mathbbm{P}^{2}} and N≥9N\geq 9, the ample line bundle 𝒪ℙ2​(1)\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1) has maximal multipoint Seshadri constant at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N}, i.e. ϵS​(𝒪ℙ2​(1),N)=1/N\epsilon_{S}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1);N)=1/\sqrt{N} where to simplify the notation we did not report the points since they are very general. Thanks to Theorems A, B, we can then read the Nagata’s conjecture in the following way.

Conjecture 6.12 ([Nag58], Nagata’s Conjecture).

For N≥9N\geq 9 very general points in ℙ2\mathbbm{P}^{2}, let {Δj​(𝒪ℙ2​(1))}j=1N\{\Delta_{j}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1))\}_{j=1}^{N} be the multipoint Okounkov bodies calculated from a family of valuations νpj\nu^{p_{j}} associated to a family of infinitesimal flags centered respectively at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N}. Then the following equivalent statements hold:

  • i)

    ϵS​(𝒪ℙ2​(1),N)=1/N\epsilon_{S}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1);N)=1/\sqrt{N};

  • ii)

    Δj​(𝒪ℙ2​(1))=1N​Σ2\Delta_{j}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1))=\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\Sigma_{2}, where Σ2\Sigma_{2} is the standard 2−2-symplex;

  • iii)

    Ωj​(𝒪ℙ2​(1))=B1N​(0)\Omega_{j}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1))=B_{\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}}(0);

Remark 6.13.

It is well know that the conjecture holds if N≥9N\geq 9 is a perfect square. And a similar conjecture (called Biran-Nagata-Szemberg’s conjecture) claims that for any ample line bundle LL on a projective manifold of dimension nn there exist N0=N0​(X,L)N_{0}=N_{0}(X,L) big enough such that ϵS​(L,N)=LnNn\epsilon_{S}(L;N)=\sqrt[n]{\frac{L^{n}}{N}} for any N≥N0N\geq N_{0} very general points, i.e. it is maximal. This conjecture can be similarly read through the multipoint Okounkov bodies as Δj​(L)=LnNn​Σn\Delta_{j}(L)=\sqrt[n]{\frac{L^{n}}{N}}\Sigma_{n} for any N≥N0N\geq N_{0} very general points at XX.

Theorem 6.14.

For N≥9N\geq 9 very general points in ℙ2\mathbbm{P}^{2}, there exists a family of valuations νpj\nu^{p_{j}} associated to a family of infinitesimal flags centered respectively at p1,…,pNp_{1},\dots,p_{N} such that

Δj​(𝒪ℙ2​(1))={(x,y)∈ℝ2: 0≤x≤ϵ​and​  0≤y≤1N​ϵ​(1−xϵ)}=C​o​n​v​(0→,ϵ​e→1,1N​ϵ​e→2)\Delta_{j}\Big(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1)\Big)=\bigg\{(x,y)\in\mathbbm{R}^{2}\,:\,0\leq x\leq\epsilon\,\,\mathrm{and}\,\,0\leq y\leq\frac{1}{N\epsilon}\Big(1-\frac{x}{\epsilon}\Big)\bigg\}=Conv\big(\vec{0},\epsilon\vec{e}_{1},\frac{1}{N\epsilon}\vec{e}_{2}\big)

where ϵ:=ϵS​(𝒪ℙ2​(1),N)\epsilon:=\epsilon_{S}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1);N). In particular μ⁡(L,𝔼)=1N​ϵ\mu(L,\mathbbm{E})=\frac{1}{N\epsilon} and

OPENVolX|Ej​(f∗​𝒪ℙ2​(1)−t​𝔼))={tif0≤t≤ϵϵ1N​ϵ−ϵ​(1N​ϵ−t)ifϵ≤t≤1N​ϵ\mathrm{Vol}_{X|E_{j}}(f^{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1)-t\mathbbm{E}))=\,\begin{cases}t\quad\quad\mathrm{if}\quad 0\leq t\leq\epsilon\\ \frac{\epsilon}{\frac{1}{N\epsilon}-\epsilon}\Big(\frac{1}{N\epsilon}-t\Big)\quad\mathrm{if}\quad\epsilon\leq t\leq\frac{1}{N\epsilon}\end{cases}

where f:X=Bl{p1,…,pN}​ℙ2→Xf:X=\mathrm{Bl}_{\{p_{1},\dots,p_{N}\}}\mathbbm{P}^{2}\to X is the blow-up at Z={p1,…,pN}Z=\{p_{1},\dots,p_{N}\}, E1,…,ENE_{1},\dots,E_{N} the exceptional divisors and 𝔼=∑j=1NEj\mathbbm{E}=\sum_{j=1}^{N}E_{j}.

Proof.

If ϵS​(𝒪ℙ2​(1),N)=1/N\epsilon_{S}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1);N)=1/\sqrt{N}, i.e. maximal, then Δj​(𝒪ℙ2​(1))=1N​Σ2{\Delta_{j}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1))=\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\Sigma_{2}} as a consequence of Theorem A and Theorem B. Thus we may assume ϵS​(𝒪ℙ2​(1),N)<1/N\epsilon_{S}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1);N)<1/{\sqrt{N}}, and we know that there exists C=γ​H−∑j=1Nmj​Ej{C=\gamma H-\sum_{j=1}^{N}m_{j}E_{j}} sub-maximal curve, i.e. an irreducible curve such that ϵS​(𝒪ℙ2​(1),N)=γM{\epsilon_{S}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1);N)=\frac{\gamma}{M}} where M:=∑j=1NmjM:=\sum_{j=1}^{N}m_{j}. Moreover, since the points are very general, for any cycle σ\sigma of lenght NN there exists a curve Cσ=γ​H−∑j=1Nmσ⁡(j)​EjC_{\sigma}=\gamma H-\sum_{j=1}^{N}m_{\sigma(j)}E_{j}. This yields μ⁡(f∗​𝒪ℙ2​(1),𝔼)≥MN​γ=1N​ϵ\mu(f^{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1);\mathbbm{E})\geq\frac{M}{N\gamma}=\frac{1}{N\epsilon} since we can easily construct a section s∈H0​(ℙ2,𝒪ℙ2​(N​γ))s\in H^{0}\big(\mathbbm{P}^{2},\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(N\gamma)\big) such that ordpj​(s)=M\mathrm{ord}_{p_{j}}(s)=M for any jj. Recall that μ⁡(f∗​𝒪ℙ2​(1),𝔼)=sup{t≥0:f∗​𝒪ℙ2​(1)−t​𝔼​is​big}\mu(f^{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1);\mathbbm{E})=\sup\{t\geq 0\,:\,f^{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1)-t\mathbbm{E}\,\mathrm{is}\,\mathrm{big}\}. Moreover for any j=1,…,Nj=1,\dots,N we can fix holomorphic coordinates (z1,j,z2,j)(z_{1,j},z_{2,j}) such that νpj​(s)=(0,M)\nu^{p_{j}}(s)=(0,M) with respect to the deglex order. So, considering an ample line bundle AA such that there exist sections s1,…,sN∈H0​(X,A)s_{1},\dots,s_{N}\in H^{0}(X,A) with νpj​(sj)=(0,0)\nu^{p_{j}}(s_{j})=(0,0) and νpi​(sj)>0\nu^{p_{i}}(s_{j})>0 for any i≠ji\neq j, we get sl⊗sjN​γ∈VN​γ,j​(l​L+A)s^{l}\otimes s_{j}^{N\gamma}\in V_{N\gamma,j}(lL+A), i.e. (0,MN​γ)=(0,1N​ϵ)∈Δj​(L+1l​A)(0,\frac{M}{N\gamma})=(0,\frac{1}{N\epsilon})\in\Delta_{j}(L+\frac{1}{l}A) by homogeneity (Proposition 3.10), for any l∈ℕl\in\mathbbm{N} and any j=1,…,Nj=1,\dots,N. Hence by Theorem 3.15 we deduce (0,MN​γ)∈Δj​(L)(0,\frac{M}{N\gamma})\in\Delta_{j}(L) for any j=1,…,Nj=1,\dots,N.
Finally since by Theorem B we know that ϵS​(𝒪ℙ2​(1),N)​Σ2⊂Δj​(L)\epsilon_{S}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1);N)\Sigma_{2}\subset\Delta_{j}(L) for any j=1​…,Nj=1\dots,N, Theorem A and the convexity imply that the multipoint Okounkov bodies have necessarily the shape requested. ∎

Corollary 6.15.

The ray f∗​𝒪ℙ2​(1)−t​𝔼f^{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1)-t\mathbbm{E} meet at most two Zariski chambers.

Corollary 6.15 was already proved in Proposition 2.5. of [DKMS15].

Remark 6.16.

We recall that Biran in [Bir97] gave an homological criterion to check if a 4−4-dimensional symplectic manifold admits a full symplectic packings by NN equal balls for large NN, showing that (ℙ2,ωF​S)(\mathbbm{P}^{2},\omega_{FS}) admits a full symplectic packings for N≥9N\geq 9. Moreover it is well-known that for any N≤9N\leq 9 the supremum over all rr such that {(Br​(0),ωs​t)}j=1N\{(B_{r}(0),\omega_{st})\}_{j=1}^{N} packs into (ℙ2,𝒪ℙ2​(1))(\mathbbm{P}^{2},\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1)) coincides with the supremum over all rr such that (ℙ2,ωF​S)(\mathbbm{P}^{2},\omega_{FS}) admits a symplectic packings of NN balls of radii rr (called Gromov width). Therefore by Theorem 3 and Corollary 5.15 the Nagata’s conjecture is true iff the Gromov width of NN balls on (ℙ2,ωF​S)(\mathbbm{P}^{2},\omega_{FS}) coincides with the multipoint Seshadri constant of 𝒪ℙ2​(1)\mathcal{O}_{\mathbbm{P}^{2}}(1) at NN very general points.

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for all.

Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a list of packages that need conversion, and welcome developer contributions.
